content.en:
GenAI-3 BUILD: AI SaaS Product

Build a Text Composition & Rewriting SaaS

Build ProseAI — a production-ready text rewriting and composition service with multiple modes: summarize, expand, simplify, change tone, and translate style. Python + FastAPI backend with streaming responses.
60 min Advanced / Hands-On You will build and deploy a real product

What You Will Build

In this lesson you build ProseAI — a text rewriting and composition SaaS. Users submit text and choose a rewriting mode (summarize, expand, simplify, formal, casual), and your service transforms the text using LLM-powered prompt templates and a streaming response pipeline. You will implement the full stack: text analysis engine, transformation pipeline, prompt template system, streaming API, and a frontend with live preview.

ProseAI — Complete Project Overview

Component Technology
API ServerPython + FastAPI
Text AnalysisCustom readability scoring, sentence analysis
LLM IntegrationOpenAI API / Anthropic API (via prompt templates)
StreamingServer-Sent Events (SSE) via FastAPI StreamingResponse
FrontendHTML + vanilla JS with live streaming preview
DeploymentDocker + any cloud provider

Project Structure

Part 1: Text Analysis Engine

Before rewriting text, you need to understand it. The analysis engine scores readability using the Flesch Reading Ease formula (0 = very hard, 100 = very easy), measures sentence complexity, and identifies word frequency patterns. These metrics guide the transformation pipeline and give users a “before vs. after” comparison.

Python 

# analyzer.py - Text analysis engine for ProseAI

import re
from collections import Counter

class TextAnalyzer:
    """Analyze text for readability, complexity, and word frequency."""

    def count_syllables(self, word):
        """Estimate syllable count using vowel-group heuristic."""
        word = word.lower().strip()
        if len(word) == 0:
            return 0
        if word.endswith("e") and len(word) > 2:
            word = word[:-1]
        vowels = "aeiou"
        count = 0
        prev_vowel = False
        for ch in word:
            is_vowel = ch in vowels
            if is_vowel and not prev_vowel:
                count += 1
            prev_vowel = is_vowel
        return max(count, 1)

    def split_sentences(self, text):
        sentences = re.split(r"[.!?]+", text)
        return [s.strip() for s in sentences if s.strip()]

    def get_words(self, text):
        return re.findall(r"[a-zA-Z]+", text.lower())

    def flesch_reading_ease(self, text):
        """Flesch Reading Ease: 90-100 very easy, 0-30 very hard."""
        sentences = self.split_sentences(text)
        words = self.get_words(text)
        if not sentences or not words:
            return 0.0
        total_syl = sum(self.count_syllables(w) for w in words)
        asl = len(words) / len(sentences)
        asw = total_syl / len(words)
        score = 206.835 - (1.015 * asl) - (84.6 * asw)
        return round(max(0, min(100, score)), 1)

    def analyze(self, text):
        """Full text analysis: readability, complexity, frequency."""
        sentences = self.split_sentences(text)
        words = self.get_words(text)
        if not words:
            return {"error": "No text to analyze"}
        syl_counts = [self.count_syllables(w) for w in words]
        freq = Counter(words)
        complex_words = [w for w, s in zip(words, syl_counts) if s >= 3]
        avg_sl = len(words) / max(len(sentences), 1)
        avg_syl = sum(syl_counts) / len(words)
        grade = 0.39 * avg_sl + 11.8 * avg_syl - 15.59
        return {
            "word_count": len(words),
            "sentence_count": len(sentences),
            "avg_sentence_length": round(avg_sl, 1),
            "flesch_reading_ease": self.flesch_reading_ease(text),
            "grade_level": round(max(0, grade), 1),
            "vocabulary_richness": round(len(set(words)) / len(words), 3),
            "complex_word_pct": round(len(complex_words) / len(words) * 100, 1),
            "top_words": freq.most_common(5),
        }

    def reading_level_label(self, score):
        if score >= 80: return "Easy (6th grade or below)"
        elif score >= 60: return "Standard (8th-9th grade)"
        elif score >= 40: return "Difficult (10th-12th grade)"
        else: return "Very Difficult (College+)"


# --- Demo ---
analyzer = TextAnalyzer()

samples = {
    "Simple": (
        "The cat sat on the mat. It was a nice day. "
        "The sun was warm. Birds sang in the trees."
    ),
    "Medium": (
        "Machine learning algorithms process large datasets to identify "
        "patterns and make predictions. These systems improve their "
        "performance over time through experience."
    ),
    "Complex": (
        "The epistemological implications of artificial intelligence "
        "necessitate a fundamental reconceptualization of computational "
        "hermeneutics, particularly regarding the phenomenological "
        "intersection of algorithmic determinism and emergent cognitive "
        "architectures in contemporary technological paradigms."
    ),
}

for label, text in samples.items():
    r = analyzer.analyze(text)
    fre = r["flesch_reading_ease"]
    print(f"=== {label} Text ===")
    print(f"  Words: {r['word_count']}, Sentences: {r['sentence_count']}")
    print(f"  Avg sentence length: {r['avg_sentence_length']} words")
    print(f"  Flesch Reading Ease: {fre} ({analyzer.reading_level_label(fre)})")
    print(f"  Grade level: {r['grade_level']}")
    print(f"  Complex words: {r['complex_word_pct']}%")
    print()

Part 2: Text Transformation Pipeline

The transformation pipeline performs rule-based text processing — simplification, sentence splitting, and filler removal — without needing an LLM. This is useful as a fallback when APIs are down, for lightweight requests, and as preprocessing before LLM-based rewriting.

Python 

# transformer.py - Rule-based text transformation pipeline

import re

class TextTransformer:
    """Rule-based text transformations without LLM dependency."""

    SIMPLIFY_MAP = {
        "utilize": "use", "implement": "set up",
        "facilitate": "help", "subsequently": "then",
        "approximately": "about", "demonstrate": "show",
        "consequently": "so", "nevertheless": "still",
        "furthermore": "also", "comprehensive": "full",
        "fundamental": "basic", "methodology": "method",
        "sufficient": "enough", "necessitate": "need",
        "endeavor": "try", "commence": "start",
        "terminate": "end", "modifications": "changes",
        "functionality": "features",
    }

    FILLER_WORDS = [
        "very", "really", "basically", "actually", "literally",
        "definitely", "certainly", "absolutely", "simply",
        "quite", "rather", "somewhat", "just",
    ]

    def simplify_vocabulary(self, text):
        """Replace complex words with simpler alternatives."""
        result = text
        replacements = []
        for cw, sw in self.SIMPLIFY_MAP.items():
            pattern = re.compile(r"\\b" + cw + r"\\b", re.IGNORECASE)
            if pattern.search(result):
                def repl(m, simple=sw):
                    return simple.capitalize() if m.group(0)[0].isupper() else simple
                result = pattern.sub(repl, result)
                replacements.append(f"{cw} -> {sw}")
        return result, replacements

    def remove_fillers(self, text):
        """Remove filler words and unnecessary adverbs."""
        removed = []
        result = text
        for filler in self.FILLER_WORDS:
            pattern = re.compile(r"\\b" + filler + r"\\b\\s*", re.IGNORECASE)
            if pattern.search(result):
                result = pattern.sub("", result)
                removed.append(filler)
        return re.sub(r"\\s{2,}", " ", result).strip(), removed

    def split_long_sentences(self, text, max_words=25):
        """Break long sentences at conjunctions."""
        conjunctions = [", and ", ", but ", ", which ", "; ", ", however "]
        sentences = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\\s+", text)
        result = []
        for sentence in sentences:
            if len(sentence.split()) > max_words:
                split_done = False
                for conj in conjunctions:
                    if conj in sentence:
                        parts = sentence.split(conj, 1)
                        if len(parts[0].split()) >= 5:
                            result.append(parts[0].strip() + ".")
                            second = parts[1].strip()
                            if second and second[0].islower():
                                second = second[0].upper() + second[1:]
                            result.append(second)
                            split_done = True
                            break
                if not split_done:
                    result.append(sentence)
            else:
                result.append(sentence)
        return " ".join(result)

    def make_concise(self, text):
        """Apply all simplification rules."""
        text, vocab_changes = self.simplify_vocabulary(text)
        text, fillers_removed = self.remove_fillers(text)
        text = self.split_long_sentences(text)
        return {"text": text, "vocab_changes": vocab_changes,
                "fillers_removed": fillers_removed}


# --- Demo ---
transformer = TextTransformer()

sample = (
    "The company will subsequently utilize a very comprehensive "
    "methodology to facilitate the implementation of fundamental "
    "modifications, which will definitely demonstrate the "
    "functionality of the system, and furthermore this will "
    "basically commence a really significant transformation "
    "that will certainly necessitate approximately three months "
    "of quite intensive endeavor to terminate successfully."
)

print("=== Original Text ===")
print(sample)
print(f"Word count: {len(sample.split())}")

result = transformer.make_concise(sample)
print(f"\
=== After All Transforms ===")
print(result["text"])
print(f"Word count: {len(result['text'].split())}")
print(f"Vocabulary swaps: {result['vocab_changes']}")
print(f"Fillers removed: {result['fillers_removed']}")

Part 3: Prompt Templates for LLM-Based Rewriting

The real power of ProseAI comes from LLM-based rewriting. Each mode (summarize, formal, casual, expand, simplify) has a carefully crafted prompt template. The template system separates the system message (persona) from the instruction (task) and the user content (text to transform). Good prompt templates are your competitive advantage — the same LLM API is available to everyone, but your templates determine quality.

Python 

# prompts.py - Prompt template system for ProseAI

class PromptTemplateEngine:
    """Manages prompt templates for different rewriting modes."""

    TEMPLATES = {
        "summarize": {
            "name": "Summarize",
            "description": "Condense text to key points",
            "system": ("You are an expert summarizer. Extract the core meaning "
                       "and key points. Preserve factual accuracy."),
            "instruction": ("Summarize the following text in {length} sentences. "
                            "Keep the most important facts and conclusions."),
            "defaults": {"length": "2-3"},
        },
        "formal": {
            "name": "Formal Tone",
            "description": "Rewrite in professional, formal style",
            "system": ("You are a professional editor specializing in formal "
                       "business and academic writing."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text in a formal, professional tone. "
                            "Use precise vocabulary, avoid contractions. "
                            "Preserve all factual content."),
            "defaults": {},
        },
        "casual": {
            "name": "Casual Tone",
            "description": "Rewrite in friendly, conversational style",
            "system": ("You are a friendly writer who makes complex topics "
                       "accessible and conversational."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text in a casual, friendly tone. "
                            "Use everyday language. Do not lose any key information."),
            "defaults": {},
        },
        "expand": {
            "name": "Expand",
            "description": "Elaborate with more detail and examples",
            "system": ("You are a thorough writer who enriches content with "
                       "relevant details and examples."),
            "instruction": ("Expand the following text to approximately {target_length}. "
                            "Add relevant details and examples. "
                            "Do not add speculative information."),
            "defaults": {"target_length": "twice the original length"},
        },
        "simplify": {
            "name": "Simplify",
            "description": "Rewrite for easy reading (grade 6 level)",
            "system": ("You are a plain-language expert. Rewrite text so that "
                       "a 12-year-old can understand it."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text at a {grade} reading level. "
                            "Use short sentences (under 15 words). "
                            "Replace jargon with simple words."),
            "defaults": {"grade": "6th grade"},
        },
    }

    def build_prompt(self, mode, user_text, **kwargs):
        """Build a complete prompt for the given rewriting mode."""
        if mode not in self.TEMPLATES:
            return {"error": f"Unknown mode: {mode}"}
        t = self.TEMPLATES[mode]
        params = dict(t["defaults"])
        params.update(kwargs)
        instruction = t["instruction"].format(**params)
        return {
            "mode": mode, "mode_name": t["name"],
            "messages": [
                {"role": "system", "content": t["system"]},
                {"role": "user", "content": f"{instruction}\
\
---\
\
{user_text}"},
            ],
        }

    def list_modes(self):
        return {k: {"name": t["name"], "description": t["description"],
                     "params": list(t["defaults"].keys())}
                for k, t in self.TEMPLATES.items()}


# --- Demo ---
engine = PromptTemplateEngine()

print("=== Available Rewriting Modes ===")
for mid, info in engine.list_modes().items():
    p = f" (params: {info['params']})" if info["params"] else ""
    print(f"  {mid:12s} - {info['description']}{p}")

sample = (
    "The implementation of machine learning algorithms in production "
    "environments necessitates careful consideration of computational "
    "resources and model versioning strategies."
)
print(f"\
Input: {sample}\
")

for mode in ["summarize", "formal", "casual", "simplify"]:
    r = engine.build_prompt(mode, sample)
    user_msg = r["messages"][1]["content"]
    instr = user_msg[:user_msg.find("---")].strip()
    print(f"[{r['mode_name']}] {instr}")

# Simulated LLM outputs
print("\
=== Simulated LLM Outputs ===")
outputs = {
    "summarize": "Deploying ML models requires planning around compute and versioning.",
    "formal": ("The deployment of machine learning algorithms within production "
               "environments requires meticulous attention to resource allocation "
               "and version control."),
    "casual": ("When you put ML models into production, think about computing "
               "power and keeping track of model versions."),
    "simplify": ("When companies use smart computer programs, they need enough "
                 "computer power. They must keep track of changes."),
}
for mode, out in outputs.items():
    print(f"  [{mode.upper()}]: {out}")

Part 4: Streaming Responses

Users expect to see text appear word-by-word, like ChatGPT. Streaming dramatically improves perceived latency — instead of waiting 5 seconds for a complete response, users see the first word in under 200ms. ProseAI uses Python generators and Server-Sent Events (SSE) to stream rewritten text to the frontend in real time.

Python 

# streaming.py - Streaming response generator for ProseAI

import json
import re

class StreamingRewriter:
    """Streaming text generation using the generator pattern.
    In production, this wraps the LLM API streaming response."""

    def sse_format(self, data):
        """Format data as a Server-Sent Event string."""
        return f"data: {json.dumps(data)}\
\
"

    def stream_rewrite(self, original, rewritten, mode):
        """Full streaming pipeline: start, tokens, done."""
        # 1. Start event
        yield self.sse_format({
            "type": "start", "mode": mode,
            "original_length": len(original.split()),
        })
        # 2. Stream word by word
        words = rewritten.split()
        for i, word in enumerate(words):
            yield self.sse_format({
                "type": "token", "content": word + " ", "index": i,
            })
        # 3. Done event with statistics
        yield self.sse_format({
            "type": "done",
            "original_words": len(original.split()),
            "rewritten_words": len(words),
            "compression": round(len(words) / max(len(original.split()), 1), 2),
        })


# --- Demo ---
streamer = StreamingRewriter()

original = (
    "The implementation of machine learning algorithms in production "
    "environments necessitates careful consideration of computational "
    "resources, data pipeline architecture, and model versioning."
)
rewritten = (
    "Putting ML models into production means thinking about three things. "
    "First, you need enough computing power. Second, your data pipelines "
    "must be solid. Third, keep track of your model versions."
)

events = list(streamer.stream_rewrite(original, rewritten, "simplify"))
print(f"Total SSE events: {len(events)}")

# Parse and display
output = ""
for event_str in events:
    data = json.loads(event_str.replace("data: ", "").strip())
    if data["type"] == "start":
        print(f"[START] Mode: {data['mode']}, Input: {data['original_length']} words")
    elif data["type"] == "token":
        output += data["content"]
    elif data["type"] == "done":
        print(f"[OUTPUT] {output.strip()}")
        print(f"[DONE] {data['original_words']} -> {data['rewritten_words']} words "
              f"({data['compression']}x)")

print(f"\
Sample SSE event:\
  {events[2].strip()}")

Part 5: The FastAPI Server

This is the heart of ProseAI — the API server that ties together analysis, transformation, prompt templates, and streaming. The /api/rewrite endpoint supports both regular JSON responses and SSE streaming via StreamingResponse.

app/main.py
"""ProseAI API Server - Text Composition and Rewriting SaaS."""
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Depends, Header
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
import uuid, time, asyncio

from .config import settings
from .analyzer import TextAnalyzer
from .transformer import TextTransformer
from .prompts import PromptTemplateEngine
from .streaming import StreamingRewriter

app = FastAPI(title="ProseAI API", version="1.0.0")
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory="static"), name="static")

analyzer = TextAnalyzer()
transformer = TextTransformer()
prompt_engine = PromptTemplateEngine()
streamer = StreamingRewriter()

class RewriteRequest(BaseModel):
    text: str = Field(..., min_length=10, max_length=10000)
    mode: str = Field(default="simplify")
    stream: bool = Field(default=False)
    params: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)

class AnalyzeRequest(BaseModel):
    text: str = Field(..., min_length=10, max_length=10000)

async def get_user(x_api_key: str = Header(...)):
    if not x_api_key:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="API key required")
    return {"id": "user_1", "tier": "pro"}

@app.get("/api/modes")
async def list_modes():
    return {"modes": prompt_engine.list_modes()}

@app.post("/api/analyze")
async def analyze_text(req: AnalyzeRequest):
    result = analyzer.analyze(req.text)
    result["reading_level"] = analyzer.reading_level_label(
        result["flesch_reading_ease"])
    return result

@app.post("/api/rewrite")
async def rewrite_text(req: RewriteRequest, user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Rewrite text in the specified mode. Supports streaming via SSE."""
    prompt_data = prompt_engine.build_prompt(req.mode, req.text, **req.params)
    if "error" in prompt_data:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=prompt_data["error"])

    if req.stream:
        async def event_generator():
            # In production: stream from LLM API using prompt_data
            result = transformer.make_concise(req.text)
            for event in streamer.stream_rewrite(
                    req.text, result["text"], req.mode):
                yield event
                await asyncio.sleep(0.02)
        return StreamingResponse(event_generator(),
            media_type="text/event-stream",
            headers={"Cache-Control": "no-cache", "X-Accel-Buffering": "no"})

    # Non-streaming: return complete JSON response
    start = time.time()
    result = transformer.make_concise(req.text)
    return {
        "id": str(uuid.uuid4()), "mode": req.mode,
        "rewritten_text": result["text"],
        "analysis_before": analyzer.analyze(req.text),
        "analysis_after": analyzer.analyze(result["text"]),
        "processing_time": round(time.time() - start, 3),
    }

@app.get("/api/health")
async def health():
    return {"status": "ok", "service": "proseai"}

Part 7: Frontend with Live Preview

The frontend lets users paste text, choose a rewriting mode, and see the rewritten output streamed in real time. The key UX feature is the split-pane view: original text on the left, rewritten text appearing word-by-word on the right. The frontend reads SSE events using the Fetch API’s ReadableStream.

Part 13: Rate Limiting & API Protection

Every production SaaS needs rate limiting to prevent abuse, control costs, and ensure fair usage. Here is a production-grade implementation:

rate_limiter.py — Production Rate Limiting for ProseAI
"""
Production rate limiting for ProseAI.
Three tiers: in-memory (development), Redis (production), token bucket (advanced).
"""
import time
from collections import defaultdict

# === TIER 1: In-Memory Rate Limiter (Development) ===
class InMemoryRateLimiter:
    """Simple sliding window rate limiter. Works for single-server setup."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.requests = defaultdict(list)

    def is_allowed(self, key, max_requests, window_seconds):
        """Check if request is allowed under the rate limit."""
        now = time.time()
        window_start = now - window_seconds

        # Clean old entries
        self.requests[key] = [t for t in self.requests[key] if t > window_start]

        if len(self.requests[key]) >= max_requests:
            retry_after = self.requests[key][0] - window_start
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "limit": max_requests,
                "window": window_seconds,
                "retry_after": round(retry_after, 1),
                "current": len(self.requests[key])
            }}

        self.requests[key].append(now)
        return True, {{
            "remaining": max_requests - len(self.requests[key]),
            "limit": max_requests,
            "reset": round(window_start + window_seconds - now, 1)
        }}

# === TIER 2: Redis Rate Limiter (Production) ===
class RedisRateLimiter:
    """Redis-based rate limiter for distributed deployments.

    In production, install: pip install redis
    And use a real Redis connection.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        # In production: self.redis = redis.Redis(host='redis', port=6379, db=0)
        self.memory = defaultdict(list)  # Simulating Redis

    def check_rate_limit(self, user_id, tier="free"):
        """Check rate limit based on user tier."""
        limits = {{
            "free":       {{"requests_per_minute": 5,  "requests_per_day": 50}},
            "starter":    {{"requests_per_minute": 20, "requests_per_day": 500}},
            "pro":        {{"requests_per_minute": 60, "requests_per_day": 5000}},
            "enterprise": {{"requests_per_minute": 200, "requests_per_day": 50000}},
        }}

        tier_limits = limits.get(tier, limits["free"])
        now = time.time()

        # Check per-minute limit
        minute_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:minute"
        self.memory[minute_key] = [t for t in self.memory[minute_key] if t > now - 60]

        if len(self.memory[minute_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_minute"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_minute",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"],
                "retry_after_seconds": 60 - (now - self.memory[minute_key][0])
            }}

        # Check per-day limit
        day_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:day"
        self.memory[day_key] = [t for t in self.memory[day_key] if t > now - 86400]

        if len(self.memory[day_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_day"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "daily_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_day",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_day"],
            }}

        # Allow request
        self.memory[minute_key].append(now)
        self.memory[day_key].append(now)

        return True, {{
            "remaining_minute": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"] - len(self.memory[minute_key]),
            "remaining_day": tier_limits["requests_per_day"] - len(self.memory[day_key]),
        }}

# === FastAPI Middleware ===
class RateLimitMiddleware:
    """
    FastAPI middleware for rate limiting.

    Usage in your app:
        from rate_limiter import RateLimitMiddleware
        app.add_middleware(RateLimitMiddleware)

    Or as a dependency:
        @app.get("/generate")
        async def generate(rate_limit: dict = Depends(check_rate_limit)):
            ...
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.limiter = RedisRateLimiter()

    def get_middleware_code(self):
        """Print the actual FastAPI middleware code."""
        code = "# Add to your FastAPI app:\
\
"
        code += "from fastapi import Request, Response\
"
        code += "from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware\
\
"
        code += "class RateLimitMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):\
"
        code += "    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):\
"
        code += "        api_key = request.headers.get('X-API-Key', 'anonymous')\
"
        code += "        user_id = self.get_user_from_key(api_key)\
"
        code += "        tier = self.get_user_tier(user_id)\
"
        code += "        allowed, info = self.limiter.check_rate_limit(user_id, tier)\
"
        code += "        if not allowed:\
"
        code += "            return JSONResponse(status_code=429, content=info)\
"
        code += "        response = await call_next(request)\
"
        code += "        response.headers['X-RateLimit-Remaining'] = str(info.get('remaining_minute', 0))\
"
        code += "        return response\
"
        print(code)

Key Takeaways

  • Analyze before you transform: Measuring readability, sentence complexity, and word frequency gives you objective metrics. It lets you show users a “before vs. after” comparison that proves your service adds value.
  • Rule-based transforms are your safety net: Vocabulary simplification, filler removal, and sentence splitting work offline and cost nothing. Use them as fallbacks when LLM APIs are down.
  • Prompt templates are your moat: The same LLM API is available to everyone. Your carefully crafted prompt templates — with system messages, instructions, and constraints — determine quality and consistency.
  • Streaming is mandatory for text products: Users will not wait 5–10 seconds staring at a spinner. Streaming word-by-word via SSE makes the product feel instant and engaging.
  • Separate concerns cleanly: Analyzer, Transformer, PromptEngine, and Streamer are independent modules. Each can be tested, replaced, or upgraded without touching the others.

Partea 1: Motorul de analiză a textului

Înainte de a rescrie textul, trebuie să-l înțelegi. Motorul de analiză calculează lizibilitatea folosind formula Flesch Reading Ease (0 = foarte greu, 100 = foarte ușor), măsoară complexitatea propozițiilor și identifică tiparele de frecvență a cuvintelor. Aceste metrici ghidează pipeline-ul de transformare și oferă utilizatorilor o comparație “înainte vs. după”.

Python 

# analyzer.py - Text analysis engine for ProseAI

import re
from collections import Counter

class TextAnalyzer:
    """Analyze text for readability, complexity, and word frequency."""

    def count_syllables(self, word):
        """Estimate syllable count using vowel-group heuristic."""
        word = word.lower().strip()
        if len(word) == 0:
            return 0
        if word.endswith("e") and len(word) > 2:
            word = word[:-1]
        vowels = "aeiou"
        count = 0
        prev_vowel = False
        for ch in word:
            is_vowel = ch in vowels
            if is_vowel and not prev_vowel:
                count += 1
            prev_vowel = is_vowel
        return max(count, 1)

    def split_sentences(self, text):
        sentences = re.split(r"[.!?]+", text)
        return [s.strip() for s in sentences if s.strip()]

    def get_words(self, text):
        return re.findall(r"[a-zA-Z]+", text.lower())

    def flesch_reading_ease(self, text):
        """Flesch Reading Ease: 90-100 very easy, 0-30 very hard."""
        sentences = self.split_sentences(text)
        words = self.get_words(text)
        if not sentences or not words:
            return 0.0
        total_syl = sum(self.count_syllables(w) for w in words)
        asl = len(words) / len(sentences)
        asw = total_syl / len(words)
        score = 206.835 - (1.015 * asl) - (84.6 * asw)
        return round(max(0, min(100, score)), 1)

    def analyze(self, text):
        """Full text analysis: readability, complexity, frequency."""
        sentences = self.split_sentences(text)
        words = self.get_words(text)
        if not words:
            return {"error": "No text to analyze"}
        syl_counts = [self.count_syllables(w) for w in words]
        freq = Counter(words)
        complex_words = [w for w, s in zip(words, syl_counts) if s >= 3]
        avg_sl = len(words) / max(len(sentences), 1)
        avg_syl = sum(syl_counts) / len(words)
        grade = 0.39 * avg_sl + 11.8 * avg_syl - 15.59
        return {
            "word_count": len(words),
            "sentence_count": len(sentences),
            "avg_sentence_length": round(avg_sl, 1),
            "flesch_reading_ease": self.flesch_reading_ease(text),
            "grade_level": round(max(0, grade), 1),
            "vocabulary_richness": round(len(set(words)) / len(words), 3),
            "complex_word_pct": round(len(complex_words) / len(words) * 100, 1),
            "top_words": freq.most_common(5),
        }

    def reading_level_label(self, score):
        if score >= 80: return "Easy (6th grade or below)"
        elif score >= 60: return "Standard (8th-9th grade)"
        elif score >= 40: return "Difficult (10th-12th grade)"
        else: return "Very Difficult (College+)"

Partea 2: Pipeline-ul de transformare a textului

Pipeline-ul de transformare efectuează procesare text bazată pe reguli — simplificare, împărțirea propozițiilor și eliminarea cuvintelor de umplutură — fără a necesita un LLM. Acest lucru este util ca soluție de rezervă când API-urile sunt indisponibile, pentru cereri ușoare și ca preprocesare înainte de rescrierea bazată pe LLM.

Python 

# transformer.py - Rule-based text transformation pipeline

import re

class TextTransformer:
    """Rule-based text transformations without LLM dependency."""

    SIMPLIFY_MAP = {
        "utilize": "use", "implement": "set up",
        "facilitate": "help", "subsequently": "then",
        "approximately": "about", "demonstrate": "show",
        "consequently": "so", "nevertheless": "still",
        "furthermore": "also", "comprehensive": "full",
        "fundamental": "basic", "methodology": "method",
        "sufficient": "enough", "necessitate": "need",
        "endeavor": "try", "commence": "start",
        "terminate": "end", "modifications": "changes",
        "functionality": "features",
    }

    FILLER_WORDS = [
        "very", "really", "basically", "actually", "literally",
        "definitely", "certainly", "absolutely", "simply",
        "quite", "rather", "somewhat", "just",
    ]

    def simplify_vocabulary(self, text):
        """Replace complex words with simpler alternatives."""
        result = text
        replacements = []
        for cw, sw in self.SIMPLIFY_MAP.items():
            pattern = re.compile(r"\\b" + cw + r"\\b", re.IGNORECASE)
            if pattern.search(result):
                def repl(m, simple=sw):
                    return simple.capitalize() if m.group(0)[0].isupper() else simple
                result = pattern.sub(repl, result)
                replacements.append(f"{cw} -> {sw}")
        return result, replacements

    def remove_fillers(self, text):
        """Remove filler words and unnecessary adverbs."""
        removed = []
        result = text
        for filler in self.FILLER_WORDS:
            pattern = re.compile(r"\\b" + filler + r"\\b\\s*", re.IGNORECASE)
            if pattern.search(result):
                result = pattern.sub("", result)
                removed.append(filler)
        return re.sub(r"\\s{2,}", " ", result).strip(), removed

    def split_long_sentences(self, text, max_words=25):
        """Break long sentences at conjunctions."""
        conjunctions = [", and ", ", but ", ", which ", "; ", ", however "]
        sentences = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\\s+", text)
        result = []
        for sentence in sentences:
            if len(sentence.split()) > max_words:
                split_done = False
                for conj in conjunctions:
                    if conj in sentence:
                        parts = sentence.split(conj, 1)
                        if len(parts[0].split()) >= 5:
                            result.append(parts[0].strip() + ".")
                            second = parts[1].strip()
                            if second and second[0].islower():
                                second = second[0].upper() + second[1:]
                            result.append(second)
                            split_done = True
                            break
                if not split_done:
                    result.append(sentence)
            else:
                result.append(sentence)
        return " ".join(result)

    def make_concise(self, text):
        """Apply all simplification rules."""
        text, vocab_changes = self.simplify_vocabulary(text)
        text, fillers_removed = self.remove_fillers(text)
        text = self.split_long_sentences(text)
        return {"text": text, "vocab_changes": vocab_changes,
                "fillers_removed": fillers_removed}

Partea 3: Șabloane de prompt pentru rescrierea bazată pe LLM

Adevărata putere a ProseAI vine din rescrierea bazată pe LLM. Fiecare mod (rezumare, formal, casual, expandare, simplificare) are un șablon de prompt elaborat cu grijă. Sistemul de șabloane separă mesajul de sistem (persona) de instrucțiune (sarcina) și conținutul utilizatorului (textul de transformat). Șabloanele bune de prompt sunt avantajul tău competitiv — același API LLM este disponibil pentru toată lumea, dar șabloanele tale determină calitatea.

Python 

# prompts.py - Prompt template system for ProseAI

class PromptTemplateEngine:
    """Manages prompt templates for different rewriting modes."""

    TEMPLATES = {
        "summarize": {
            "name": "Summarize",
            "description": "Condense text to key points",
            "system": ("You are an expert summarizer. Extract the core meaning "
                       "and key points. Preserve factual accuracy."),
            "instruction": ("Summarize the following text in {length} sentences. "
                            "Keep the most important facts and conclusions."),
            "defaults": {"length": "2-3"},
        },
        "formal": {
            "name": "Formal Tone",
            "description": "Rewrite in professional, formal style",
            "system": ("You are a professional editor specializing in formal "
                       "business and academic writing."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text in a formal, professional tone. "
                            "Use precise vocabulary, avoid contractions. "
                            "Preserve all factual content."),
            "defaults": {},
        },
        "casual": {
            "name": "Casual Tone",
            "description": "Rewrite in friendly, conversational style",
            "system": ("You are a friendly writer who makes complex topics "
                       "accessible and conversational."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text in a casual, friendly tone. "
                            "Use everyday language. Do not lose any key information."),
            "defaults": {},
        },
        "expand": {
            "name": "Expand",
            "description": "Elaborate with more detail and examples",
            "system": ("You are a thorough writer who enriches content with "
                       "relevant details and examples."),
            "instruction": ("Expand the following text to approximately {target_length}. "
                            "Add relevant details and examples. "
                            "Do not add speculative information."),
            "defaults": {"target_length": "twice the original length"},
        },
        "simplify": {
            "name": "Simplify",
            "description": "Rewrite for easy reading (grade 6 level)",
            "system": ("You are a plain-language expert. Rewrite text so that "
                       "a 12-year-old can understand it."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text at a {grade} reading level. "
                            "Use short sentences (under 15 words). "
                            "Replace jargon with simple words."),
            "defaults": {"grade": "6th grade"},
        },
    }

    def build_prompt(self, mode, user_text, **kwargs):
        """Build a complete prompt for the given rewriting mode."""
        if mode not in self.TEMPLATES:
            return {"error": f"Unknown mode: {mode}"}
        t = self.TEMPLATES[mode]
        params = dict(t["defaults"])
        params.update(kwargs)
        instruction = t["instruction"].format(**params)
        return {
            "mode": mode, "mode_name": t["name"],
            "messages": [
                {"role": "system", "content": t["system"]},
                {"role": "user", "content": f"{instruction}\
\
---\
\
{user_text}"},
            ],
        }

    def list_modes(self):

Partea 4: Răspunsuri în streaming

Utilizatorii se așteaptă să vadă textul apărând cuvânt cu cuvânt, ca la ChatGPT. Streaming-ul îmbunătățește dramatic latența percepută — în loc să aștepte 5 secunde pentru un răspuns complet, utilizatorii văd primul cuvânt în mai puțin de 200ms. ProseAI folosește generatoare Python și Server-Sent Events (SSE) pentru a transmite textul rescris către frontend în timp real.

Python 

# streaming.py - Streaming response generator for ProseAI

import json
import re

class StreamingRewriter:
    """Streaming text generation using the generator pattern.
    In production, this wraps the LLM API streaming response."""

    def sse_format(self, data):
        """Format data as a Server-Sent Event string."""
        return f"data: {json.dumps(data)}\
\
"

    def stream_rewrite(self, original, rewritten, mode):
        """Full streaming pipeline: start, tokens, done."""
        # 1. Start event
        yield self.sse_format({
            "type": "start", "mode": mode,
            "original_length": len(original.split()),
        })
        # 2. Stream word by word
        words = rewritten.split()
        for i, word in enumerate(words):
            yield self.sse_format({
                "type": "token", "content": word + " ", "index": i,
            })
        # 3. Done event with statistics
        yield self.sse_format({
            "type": "done",
            "original_words": len(original.split()),
            "rewritten_words": len(words),
            "compression": round(len(words) / max(len(original.split()), 1), 2),
        })


# --- Demo ---
streamer = StreamingRewriter()

original = (
    "The implementation of machine learning algorithms in production "
    "environments necessitates careful consideration of computational "
    "resources, data pipeline architecture, and model versioning."
)
rewritten = (
    "Putting ML models into production means thinking about three things. "
    "First, you need enough computing power. Second, your data pipelines "
    "must be solid. Third, keep track of your model versions."
)

events = list(streamer.stream_rewrite(original, rewritten, "simplify"))
print(f"Total SSE events: {len(events)}")

# Parse and display
output = ""
for event_str in events:
    data = json.loads(event_str.replace("data: ", "").strip())
    if data["type"] == "start":
        print(f"[START] Mode: {data['mode']}, Input: {data['original_length']} words")
    elif data["type"] == "token":
        output += data["content"]
    elif data["type"] == "done":
        print(f"[OUTPUT] {output.strip()}")
        print(f"[DONE] {data['original_words']} -> {data['rewritten_words']} words "
              f"({data['compression']}x)")

print(f"\

"""ProseAI API Server - Text Composition and Rewriting SaaS."""
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Depends, Header
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
import uuid, time, asyncio

from .config import settings
from .analyzer import TextAnalyzer
from .transformer import TextTransformer
from .prompts import PromptTemplateEngine
from .streaming import StreamingRewriter

app = FastAPI(title="ProseAI API", version="1.0.0")
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory="static"), name="static")

analyzer = TextAnalyzer()
transformer = TextTransformer()
prompt_engine = PromptTemplateEngine()
streamer = StreamingRewriter()

class RewriteRequest(BaseModel):
    text: str = Field(..., min_length=10, max_length=10000)
    mode: str = Field(default="simplify")
    stream: bool = Field(default=False)
    params: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)

class AnalyzeRequest(BaseModel):
    text: str = Field(..., min_length=10, max_length=10000)

async def get_user(x_api_key: str = Header(...)):
    if not x_api_key:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="API key required")
    return {"id": "user_1", "tier": "pro"}

@app.get("/api/modes")
async def list_modes():
    return {"modes": prompt_engine.list_modes()}

@app.post("/api/analyze")
async def analyze_text(req: AnalyzeRequest):
    result = analyzer.analyze(req.text)
    result["reading_level"] = analyzer.reading_level_label(
        result["flesch_reading_ease"])
    return result

@app.post("/api/rewrite")
async def rewrite_text(req: RewriteRequest, user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Rewrite text in the specified mode. Supports streaming via SSE."""
    prompt_data = prompt_engine.build_prompt(req.mode, req.text, **req.params)
    if "error" in prompt_data:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=prompt_data["error"])

    if req.stream:
        async def event_generator():
            # In production: stream from LLM API using prompt_data
            result = transformer.make_concise(req.text)
            for event in streamer.stream_rewrite(
                    req.text, result["text"], req.mode):
                yield event
                await asyncio.sleep(0.02)
        return StreamingResponse(event_generator(),
            media_type="text/event-stream",
            headers={"Cache-Control": "no-cache", "X-Accel-Buffering": "no"})

    # Non-streaming: return complete JSON response
    start = time.time()
    result = transformer.make_concise(req.text)
    return {
        "id": str(uuid.uuid4()), "mode": req.mode,
        "rewritten_text": result["text"],
        "analysis_before": analyzer.analyze(req.text),
        "analysis_after": analyzer.analyze(result["text"]),
        "processing_time": round(time.time() - start, 3),
    }

@app.get("/api/health")
async def health():
    return {"status": "ok", "service": "proseai"}

Partea 11: Conectare la Propriul LLM

Până acum am folosit API-uri terțe. Dar puterea reală — și marjele reale — vin când rulezi propriile modele. Aceasta elimină costurile API per cerere, îți oferă control total asupra latenței și confidențialității, și îți permite să ajustezi modelele pentru cazul tău specific de utilizare.

Trei abordări principale pentru auto-hosting:

  • vLLM — cel mai mare debit, API compatibil OpenAI, ideal pentru producție
  • Ollama — cea mai ușoară configurare, ideal pentru dezvoltare și deployment la scară mică
  • llama.cpp — cel mai ușor, rulează pe CPU, ideal pentru deployment la margine

Pentru generarea de text, auto-găzduiește cu vLLM, llama.cpp sau Ollama:

Partea 13: Limitarea Ratei & Protecția API

Fiecare SaaS de producție necesită limitarea ratei pentru a preveni abuzul, controla costurile și asigura utilizarea echitabilă. Iată o implementare de nivel producție:

rate_limiter.py — Production Rate Limiting for ProseAI
"""
Production rate limiting for ProseAI.
Three tiers: in-memory (development), Redis (production), token bucket (advanced).
"""
import time
from collections import defaultdict

# === TIER 1: In-Memory Rate Limiter (Development) ===
class InMemoryRateLimiter:
    """Simple sliding window rate limiter. Works for single-server setup."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.requests = defaultdict(list)

    def is_allowed(self, key, max_requests, window_seconds):
        """Check if request is allowed under the rate limit."""
        now = time.time()
        window_start = now - window_seconds

        # Clean old entries
        self.requests[key] = [t for t in self.requests[key] if t > window_start]

        if len(self.requests[key]) >= max_requests:
            retry_after = self.requests[key][0] - window_start
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "limit": max_requests,
                "window": window_seconds,
                "retry_after": round(retry_after, 1),
                "current": len(self.requests[key])
            }}

        self.requests[key].append(now)
        return True, {{
            "remaining": max_requests - len(self.requests[key]),
            "limit": max_requests,
            "reset": round(window_start + window_seconds - now, 1)
        }}

# === TIER 2: Redis Rate Limiter (Production) ===
class RedisRateLimiter:
    """Redis-based rate limiter for distributed deployments.

    In production, install: pip install redis
    And use a real Redis connection.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        # In production: self.redis = redis.Redis(host='redis', port=6379, db=0)
        self.memory = defaultdict(list)  # Simulating Redis

    def check_rate_limit(self, user_id, tier="free"):
        """Check rate limit based on user tier."""
        limits = {{
            "free":       {{"requests_per_minute": 5,  "requests_per_day": 50}},
            "starter":    {{"requests_per_minute": 20, "requests_per_day": 500}},
            "pro":        {{"requests_per_minute": 60, "requests_per_day": 5000}},
            "enterprise": {{"requests_per_minute": 200, "requests_per_day": 50000}},
        }}

        tier_limits = limits.get(tier, limits["free"])
        now = time.time()

        # Check per-minute limit
        minute_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:minute"
        self.memory[minute_key] = [t for t in self.memory[minute_key] if t > now - 60]

        if len(self.memory[minute_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_minute"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_minute",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"],
                "retry_after_seconds": 60 - (now - self.memory[minute_key][0])
            }}

        # Check per-day limit
        day_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:day"
        self.memory[day_key] = [t for t in self.memory[day_key] if t > now - 86400]

        if len(self.memory[day_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_day"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "daily_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_day",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_day"],
            }}

        # Allow request
        self.memory[minute_key].append(now)
        self.memory[day_key].append(now)

        return True, {{
            "remaining_minute": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"] - len(self.memory[minute_key]),
            "remaining_day": tier_limits["requests_per_day"] - len(self.memory[day_key]),
        }}

# === FastAPI Middleware ===
class RateLimitMiddleware:
    """
    FastAPI middleware for rate limiting.

    Usage in your app:
        from rate_limiter import RateLimitMiddleware
        app.add_middleware(RateLimitMiddleware)

    Or as a dependency:
        @app.get("/generate")
        async def generate(rate_limit: dict = Depends(check_rate_limit)):
            ...
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.limiter = RedisRateLimiter()

    def get_middleware_code(self):
        """Print the actual FastAPI middleware code."""
        code = "# Add to your FastAPI app:\
\
"
        code += "from fastapi import Request, Response\
"
        code += "from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware\
\
"
        code += "class RateLimitMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):\
"
        code += "    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):\
"
        code += "        api_key = request.headers.get('X-API-Key', 'anonymous')\
"
        code += "        user_id = self.get_user_from_key(api_key)\
"
        code += "        tier = self.get_user_tier(user_id)\
"
        code += "        allowed, info = self.limiter.check_rate_limit(user_id, tier)\
"
        code += "        if not allowed:\
"
        code += "            return JSONResponse(status_code=429, content=info)\
"
        code += "        response = await call_next(request)\
"
        code += "        response.headers['X-RateLimit-Remaining'] = str(info.get('remaining_minute', 0))\
"
        code += "        return response\
"
        print(code)

Concluzii cheie

  • Analizează înainte de a transforma: Măsurarea lizibilității, complexității propozițiilor și frecvenței cuvintelor îți oferă metrici obiective. Îți permite să arăți utilizatorilor o comparație “înainte vs. după” care dovedește că serviciul tău adaugă valoare.
  • Transformările bazate pe reguli sunt plasa ta de siguranță: Simplificarea vocabularului, eliminarea cuvintelor de umplutură și împărțirea propozițiilor funcționează offline și nu costă nimic. Folosește-le ca soluții de rezervă când API-urile LLM sunt indisponibile.
  • Șabloanele de prompt sunt avantajul tău competitiv: Același API LLM este disponibil pentru toată lumea. Șabloanele tale de prompt elaborate cu grijă — cu mesaje de sistem, instrucțiuni și constrângeri — determină calitatea și consistența.
  • Streaming-ul este obligatoriu pentru produsele de text: Utilizatorii nu vor aștepta 5–10 secunde uitându-se la un spinner. Streaming-ul cuvânt cu cuvânt prin SSE face ca produsul să pară instantaneu și captivant.
  • Separă responsabilitățile clar: Analyzer, Transformer, PromptEngine și Streamer sunt module independente. Fiecare poate fi testat, înlocuit sau actualizat fără a le afecta pe celelalte.

Următoarea lecție: În GenAI-4, construiești un SaaS de generare de cod — gestionând transformări conștiente de sintaxă, suport multi-limbaj și sandbox-uri pentru execuție sigură a codului.

Μέρος 1: Μηχανή Ανάλυσης Κειμένου

Πριν αναδιατυπώσετε κείμενο, πρέπει να το κατανοήσετε. Η μηχανή ανάλυσης βαθμολογεί την αναγνωσιμότητα χρησιμοποιώντας τον τύπο Flesch Reading Ease (0 = πολύ δύσκολο, 100 = πολύ εύκολο), μετρά την πολυπλοκότητα των προτάσεων και εντοπίζει μοτίβα συχνότητας λέξεων. Αυτές οι μετρικές καθοδηγούν τη pipeline μετασχηματισμού και δίνουν στους χρήστες μια σύγκριση “πριν έναντι μετά”.

# analyzer.py - Text analysis engine for ProseAI

import re
from collections import Counter

class TextAnalyzer:
    """Analyze text for readability, complexity, and word frequency."""

    def count_syllables(self, word):
        """Estimate syllable count using vowel-group heuristic."""
        word = word.lower().strip()
        if len(word) == 0:
            return 0
        if word.endswith("e") and len(word) > 2:
            word = word[:-1]
        vowels = "aeiou"
        count = 0
        prev_vowel = False
        for ch in word:
            is_vowel = ch in vowels
            if is_vowel and not prev_vowel:
                count += 1
            prev_vowel = is_vowel
        return max(count, 1)

    def split_sentences(self, text):
        sentences = re.split(r"[.!?]+", text)
        return [s.strip() for s in sentences if s.strip()]

    def get_words(self, text):
        return re.findall(r"[a-zA-Z]+", text.lower())

    def flesch_reading_ease(self, text):
        """Flesch Reading Ease: 90-100 very easy, 0-30 very hard."""
        sentences = self.split_sentences(text)
        words = self.get_words(text)
        if not sentences or not words:
            return 0.0
        total_syl = sum(self.count_syllables(w) for w in words)
        asl = len(words) / len(sentences)
        asw = total_syl / len(words)
        score = 206.835 - (1.015 * asl) - (84.6 * asw)
        return round(max(0, min(100, score)), 1)

    def analyze(self, text):
        """Full text analysis: readability, complexity, frequency."""
        sentences = self.split_sentences(text)
        words = self.get_words(text)
        if not words:
            return {"error": "No text to analyze"}
        syl_counts = [self.count_syllables(w) for w in words]
        freq = Counter(words)
        complex_words = [w for w, s in zip(words, syl_counts) if s >= 3]
        avg_sl = len(words) / max(len(sentences), 1)
        avg_syl = sum(syl_counts) / len(words)
        grade = 0.39 * avg_sl + 11.8 * avg_syl - 15.59
        return {
            "word_count": len(words),
            "sentence_count": len(sentences),
            "avg_sentence_length": round(avg_sl, 1),
            "flesch_reading_ease": self.flesch_reading_ease(text),
            "grade_level": round(max(0, grade), 1),
            "vocabulary_richness": round(len(set(words)) / len(words), 3),
            "complex_word_pct": round(len(complex_words) / len(words) * 100, 1),
            "top_words": freq.most_common(5),
        }

    def reading_level_label(self, score):
        if score >= 80: return "Easy (6th grade or below)"
        elif score >= 60: return "Standard (8th-9th grade)"
        elif score >= 40: return "Difficult (10th-12th grade)"
        else: return "Very Difficult (College+)"


# --- Demo ---

samples = {

    ),

Μέρος 2: Pipeline Μετασχηματισμού Κειμένου

Η pipeline μετασχηματισμού εκτελεί επεξεργασία κειμένου βάσει κανόνων — απλοποίηση, διαχωρισμό προτάσεων και αφαίρεση περιττών λέξεων — χωρίς να χρειάζεται LLM. Αυτό είναι χρήσιμο ως εναλλακτική λύση όταν τα API δεν λειτουργούν, για ελαφρά αιτήματα, και ως προεπεξεργασία πριν την αναδιατύπωση βάσει LLM.

# transformer.py - Rule-based text transformation pipeline

import re

class TextTransformer:
    """Rule-based text transformations without LLM dependency."""

    SIMPLIFY_MAP = {
        "utilize": "use", "implement": "set up",
        "facilitate": "help", "subsequently": "then",
        "approximately": "about", "demonstrate": "show",
        "consequently": "so", "nevertheless": "still",
        "furthermore": "also", "comprehensive": "full",
        "fundamental": "basic", "methodology": "method",
        "sufficient": "enough", "necessitate": "need",
        "endeavor": "try", "commence": "start",
        "terminate": "end", "modifications": "changes",
        "functionality": "features",
    }

    FILLER_WORDS = [
        "very", "really", "basically", "actually", "literally",
        "definitely", "certainly", "absolutely", "simply",
        "quite", "rather", "somewhat", "just",
    ]

    def simplify_vocabulary(self, text):
        """Replace complex words with simpler alternatives."""
        result = text
        replacements = []
        for cw, sw in self.SIMPLIFY_MAP.items():
            pattern = re.compile(r"\\b" + cw + r"\\b", re.IGNORECASE)
            if pattern.search(result):
                def repl(m, simple=sw):
                    return simple.capitalize() if m.group(0)[0].isupper() else simple
                result = pattern.sub(repl, result)
                replacements.append(f"{cw} -> {sw}")
        return result, replacements

    def remove_fillers(self, text):
        """Remove filler words and unnecessary adverbs."""
        removed = []
        result = text
        for filler in self.FILLER_WORDS:
            pattern = re.compile(r"\\b" + filler + r"\\b\\s*", re.IGNORECASE)
            if pattern.search(result):
                result = pattern.sub("", result)
                removed.append(filler)
        return re.sub(r"\\s{2,}", " ", result).strip(), removed

    def split_long_sentences(self, text, max_words=25):
        """Break long sentences at conjunctions."""
        conjunctions = [", and ", ", but ", ", which ", "; ", ", however "]
        sentences = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\\s+", text)
        result = []
        for sentence in sentences:
            if len(sentence.split()) > max_words:
                split_done = False
                for conj in conjunctions:
                    if conj in sentence:
                        parts = sentence.split(conj, 1)
                        if len(parts[0].split()) >= 5:
                            result.append(parts[0].strip() + ".")
                            second = parts[1].strip()
                            if second and second[0].islower():
                                second = second[0].upper() + second[1:]
                            result.append(second)
                            split_done = True
                            break
                if not split_done:
                    result.append(sentence)
            else:
                result.append(sentence)
        return " ".join(result)

    def make_concise(self, text):
        """Apply all simplification rules."""
        text, vocab_changes = self.simplify_vocabulary(text)
        text, fillers_removed = self.remove_fillers(text)
        text = self.split_long_sentences(text)
        return {"text": text, "vocab_changes": vocab_changes,
                "fillers_removed": fillers_removed}

Μέρος 3: Πρότυπα Prompt για Αναδιατύπωση Βάσει LLM

Η πραγματική δύναμη του ProseAI προέρχεται από την αναδιατύπωση βάσει LLM. Κάθε λειτουργία (σύνοψη, επίσημο, ανεπίσημο, επέκταση, απλοποίηση) έχει ένα προσεκτικά σχεδιασμένο πρότυπο prompt. Το σύστημα προτύπων διαχωρίζει το μήνυμα συστήματος (περσόνα) από την οδηγία (εργασία) και το περιεχόμενο χρήστη (κείμενο προς μετασχηματισμό). Τα καλά πρότυπα prompt είναι το ανταγωνιστικό σας πλεονέκτημα — το ίδιο LLM API είναι διαθέσιμο σε όλους, αλλά τα πρότυπά σας καθορίζουν την ποιότητα.

Python 

# prompts.py - Prompt template system for ProseAI

class PromptTemplateEngine:
    """Manages prompt templates for different rewriting modes."""

    TEMPLATES = {
        "summarize": {
            "name": "Summarize",
            "description": "Condense text to key points",
            "system": ("You are an expert summarizer. Extract the core meaning "
                       "and key points. Preserve factual accuracy."),
            "instruction": ("Summarize the following text in {length} sentences. "
                            "Keep the most important facts and conclusions."),
            "defaults": {"length": "2-3"},
        },
        "formal": {
            "name": "Formal Tone",
            "description": "Rewrite in professional, formal style",
            "system": ("You are a professional editor specializing in formal "
                       "business and academic writing."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text in a formal, professional tone. "
                            "Use precise vocabulary, avoid contractions. "
                            "Preserve all factual content."),
            "defaults": {},
        },
        "casual": {
            "name": "Casual Tone",
            "description": "Rewrite in friendly, conversational style",
            "system": ("You are a friendly writer who makes complex topics "
                       "accessible and conversational."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text in a casual, friendly tone. "
                            "Use everyday language. Do not lose any key information."),
            "defaults": {},
        },
        "expand": {
            "name": "Expand",
            "description": "Elaborate with more detail and examples",
            "system": ("You are a thorough writer who enriches content with "
                       "relevant details and examples."),
            "instruction": ("Expand the following text to approximately {target_length}. "
                            "Add relevant details and examples. "
                            "Do not add speculative information."),
            "defaults": {"target_length": "twice the original length"},
        },
        "simplify": {
            "name": "Simplify",
            "description": "Rewrite for easy reading (grade 6 level)",
            "system": ("You are a plain-language expert. Rewrite text so that "
                       "a 12-year-old can understand it."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text at a {grade} reading level. "
                            "Use short sentences (under 15 words). "
                            "Replace jargon with simple words."),
            "defaults": {"grade": "6th grade"},
        },
    }

    def build_prompt(self, mode, user_text, **kwargs):
        """Build a complete prompt for the given rewriting mode."""
        if mode not in self.TEMPLATES:
            return {"error": f"Unknown mode: {mode}"}
        t = self.TEMPLATES[mode]
        params = dict(t["defaults"])
        params.update(kwargs)
        instruction = t["instruction"].format(**params)
        return {
            "mode": mode, "mode_name": t["name"],
            "messages": [
                {"role": "system", "content": t["system"]},
                {"role": "user", "content": f"{instruction}\
\
---\
\
{user_text}"},
            ],
        }

    def list_modes(self):
        return {k: {"name": t["name"], "description": t["description"],
                     "params": list(t["defaults"].keys())}
                for k, t in self.TEMPLATES.items()}

Μέρος 4: Streaming Απαντήσεις

Οι χρήστες περιμένουν να βλέπουν το κείμενο να εμφανίζεται λέξη-λέξη, όπως στο ChatGPT. Το streaming βελτιώνει δραματικά την αντιλαμβανόμενη καθυστέρηση — αντί να περιμένουν 5 δευτερόλεπτα για μια ολοκληρωμένη απάντηση, οι χρήστες βλέπουν την πρώτη λέξη σε λιγότερο από 200ms. Το ProseAI χρησιμοποιεί Python generators και Server-Sent Events (SSE) για να μεταδίδει αναδιατυπωμένο κείμενο στο frontend σε πραγματικό χρόνο.

Python 

# streaming.py - Streaming response generator for ProseAI

import json
import re

class StreamingRewriter:
    """Streaming text generation using the generator pattern.
    In production, this wraps the LLM API streaming response."""

    def sse_format(self, data):
        """Format data as a Server-Sent Event string."""
        return f"data: {json.dumps(data)}\
\
"

    def stream_rewrite(self, original, rewritten, mode):
        """Full streaming pipeline: start, tokens, done."""
        # 1. Start event
        yield self.sse_format({
            "type": "start", "mode": mode,
            "original_length": len(original.split()),
        })
        # 2. Stream word by word
        words = rewritten.split()
        for i, word in enumerate(words):
            yield self.sse_format({
                "type": "token", "content": word + " ", "index": i,
            })
        # 3. Done event with statistics
        yield self.sse_format({
            "type": "done",
            "original_words": len(original.split()),
            "rewritten_words": len(words),
            "compression": round(len(words) / max(len(original.split()), 1), 2),
        })


# --- Demo ---
streamer = StreamingRewriter()

original = (
    "The implementation of machine learning algorithms in production "
    "environments necessitates careful consideration of computational "
    "resources, data pipeline architecture, and model versioning."
)
rewritten = (
    "Putting ML models into production means thinking about three things. "
    "First, you need enough computing power. Second, your data pipelines "
    "must be solid. Third, keep track of your model versions."
)

events = list(streamer.stream_rewrite(original, rewritten, "simplify"))
print(f"Total SSE events: {len(events)}")

# Parse and display
output = ""
for event_str in events:
    data = json.loads(event_str.replace("data: ", "").strip())
    if data["type"] == "start":
        print(f"[START] Mode: {data['mode']}, Input: {data['original_length']} words")
    elif data["type"] == "token":
        output += data["content"]
    elif data["type"] == "done":
        print(f"[OUTPUT] {output.strip()}")
        print(f"[DONE] {data['original_words']} -> {data['rewritten_words']} words "
              f"({data['compression']}x)")

print(f"\
Sample SSE event:\
  {events[2].strip()}")

Μέρος 5: Ο Διακομιστής FastAPI

Αυτή είναι η καρδιά του ProseAI — ο διακομιστής API που συνδέει ανάλυση, μετασχηματισμό, πρότυπα prompt και streaming. Το endpoint /api/rewrite υποστηρίζει τόσο κανονικές JSON απαντήσεις όσο και SSE streaming μέσω StreamingResponse.

app/main.py
"""ProseAI API Server - Text Composition and Rewriting SaaS."""
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Depends, Header
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
import uuid, time, asyncio

from .config import settings
from .analyzer import TextAnalyzer
from .transformer import TextTransformer
from .prompts import PromptTemplateEngine
from .streaming import StreamingRewriter

app = FastAPI(title="ProseAI API", version="1.0.0")
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory="static"), name="static")

analyzer = TextAnalyzer()
transformer = TextTransformer()
prompt_engine = PromptTemplateEngine()
streamer = StreamingRewriter()

class RewriteRequest(BaseModel):
    text: str = Field(..., min_length=10, max_length=10000)
    mode: str = Field(default="simplify")
    stream: bool = Field(default=False)
    params: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)

class AnalyzeRequest(BaseModel):
    text: str = Field(..., min_length=10, max_length=10000)

async def get_user(x_api_key: str = Header(...)):
    if not x_api_key:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="API key required")
    return {"id": "user_1", "tier": "pro"}

@app.get("/api/modes")
async def list_modes():
    return {"modes": prompt_engine.list_modes()}

@app.post("/api/analyze")
async def analyze_text(req: AnalyzeRequest):
    result = analyzer.analyze(req.text)
    result["reading_level"] = analyzer.reading_level_label(
        result["flesch_reading_ease"])
    return result

@app.post("/api/rewrite")
async def rewrite_text(req: RewriteRequest, user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Rewrite text in the specified mode. Supports streaming via SSE."""
    prompt_data = prompt_engine.build_prompt(req.mode, req.text, **req.params)
    if "error" in prompt_data:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=prompt_data["error"])

    if req.stream:
        async def event_generator():
            # In production: stream from LLM API using prompt_data
            result = transformer.make_concise(req.text)
            for event in streamer.stream_rewrite(
                    req.text, result["text"], req.mode):
                yield event
                await asyncio.sleep(0.02)
        return StreamingResponse(event_generator(),
            media_type="text/event-stream",
            headers={"Cache-Control": "no-cache", "X-Accel-Buffering": "no"})

    # Non-streaming: return complete JSON response
    start = time.time()
    result = transformer.make_concise(req.text)
    return {
        "id": str(uuid.uuid4()), "mode": req.mode,
        "rewritten_text": result["text"],
        "analysis_before": analyzer.analyze(req.text),
        "analysis_after": analyzer.analyze(result["text"]),
        "processing_time": round(time.time() - start, 3),
    }

@app.get("/api/health")
async def health():
    return {"status": "ok", "service": "proseai"}

Μέρος 7: Frontend με Ζωντανή Προεπισκόπηση

Κάθε SaaS παραγωγής χρειάζεται περιορισμό ρυθμού για να αποτρέψει κατάχρηση, να ελέγξει κόστη και να εξασφαλίσει δίκαιη χρήση. Εδώ είναι μια υλοποίηση επιπέδου παραγωγής:

rate_limiter.py — Production Rate Limiting for ProseAI
"""
Production rate limiting for ProseAI.
Three tiers: in-memory (development), Redis (production), token bucket (advanced).
"""
import time
from collections import defaultdict

# === TIER 1: In-Memory Rate Limiter (Development) ===
class InMemoryRateLimiter:
    """Simple sliding window rate limiter. Works for single-server setup."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.requests = defaultdict(list)

    def is_allowed(self, key, max_requests, window_seconds):
        """Check if request is allowed under the rate limit."""
        now = time.time()
        window_start = now - window_seconds

        # Clean old entries
        self.requests[key] = [t for t in self.requests[key] if t > window_start]

        if len(self.requests[key]) >= max_requests:
            retry_after = self.requests[key][0] - window_start
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "limit": max_requests,
                "window": window_seconds,
                "retry_after": round(retry_after, 1),
                "current": len(self.requests[key])
            }}

        self.requests[key].append(now)
        return True, {{
            "remaining": max_requests - len(self.requests[key]),
            "limit": max_requests,
            "reset": round(window_start + window_seconds - now, 1)
        }}

# === TIER 2: Redis Rate Limiter (Production) ===
class RedisRateLimiter:
    """Redis-based rate limiter for distributed deployments.

    In production, install: pip install redis
    And use a real Redis connection.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        # In production: self.redis = redis.Redis(host='redis', port=6379, db=0)
        self.memory = defaultdict(list)  # Simulating Redis

    def check_rate_limit(self, user_id, tier="free"):
        """Check rate limit based on user tier."""
        limits = {{
            "free":       {{"requests_per_minute": 5,  "requests_per_day": 50}},
            "starter":    {{"requests_per_minute": 20, "requests_per_day": 500}},
            "pro":        {{"requests_per_minute": 60, "requests_per_day": 5000}},
            "enterprise": {{"requests_per_minute": 200, "requests_per_day": 50000}},
        }}

        tier_limits = limits.get(tier, limits["free"])
        now = time.time()

        # Check per-minute limit
        minute_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:minute"
        self.memory[minute_key] = [t for t in self.memory[minute_key] if t > now - 60]

        if len(self.memory[minute_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_minute"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_minute",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"],
                "retry_after_seconds": 60 - (now - self.memory[minute_key][0])
            }}

        # Check per-day limit
        day_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:day"
        self.memory[day_key] = [t for t in self.memory[day_key] if t > now - 86400]

        if len(self.memory[day_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_day"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "daily_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_day",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_day"],
            }}

        # Allow request
        self.memory[minute_key].append(now)
        self.memory[day_key].append(now)

        return True, {{
            "remaining_minute": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"] - len(self.memory[minute_key]),
            "remaining_day": tier_limits["requests_per_day"] - len(self.memory[day_key]),
        }}

# === FastAPI Middleware ===
class RateLimitMiddleware:
    """
    FastAPI middleware for rate limiting.

    Usage in your app:
        from rate_limiter import RateLimitMiddleware
        app.add_middleware(RateLimitMiddleware)

    Or as a dependency:
        @app.get("/generate")
        async def generate(rate_limit: dict = Depends(check_rate_limit)):
            ...
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.limiter = RedisRateLimiter()

    def get_middleware_code(self):
        """Print the actual FastAPI middleware code."""
        code = "# Add to your FastAPI app:\
\
"
        code += "from fastapi import Request, Response\
"
        code += "from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware\
\
"
        code += "class RateLimitMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):\
"
        code += "    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):\
"
        code += "        api_key = request.headers.get('X-API-Key', 'anonymous')\
"
        code += "        user_id = self.get_user_from_key(api_key)\
"
        code += "        tier = self.get_user_tier(user_id)\
"
        code += "        allowed, info = self.limiter.check_rate_limit(user_id, tier)\
"
        code += "        if not allowed:\
"
        code += "            return JSONResponse(status_code=429, content=info)\
"
        code += "        response = await call_next(request)\
"
        code += "        response.headers['X-RateLimit-Remaining'] = str(info.get('remaining_minute', 0))\
"
        code += "        return response\
"
        print(code)


# --- Demo ---
print("=== Rate Limiting Demo for ProseAI ===\
")

limiter = RedisRateLimiter()

# Simulate requests from different users
users = [
    ("user_free_1", "free"),
    ("user_pro_1", "pro"),
    ("user_enterprise_1", "enterprise"),
]

for user_id, tier in users:
    print(f"User: {{user_id}} ({{tier}} tier)")
    for i in range(8):
        allowed, info = limiter.check_rate_limit(user_id, tier)
        status = "ALLOWED" if allowed else "BLOCKED"
        print(f"  Request {{i+1}}: {{status}} | {{info}}")
        if not allowed:
            break
    print()

Βασικά Συμπεράσματα

  • Αναλύστε πριν μετασχηματίσετε: Η μέτρηση αναγνωσιμότητας, πολυπλοκότητας προτάσεων και συχνότητας λέξεων σας δίνει αντικειμενικές μετρικές. Σας επιτρέπει να δείξετε στους χρήστες μια σύγκριση “πριν έναντι μετά” που αποδεικνύει ότι η υπηρεσία σας προσθέτει αξία.
  • Οι μετασχηματισμοί βάσει κανόνων είναι το δίχτυ ασφαλείας σας: Η απλοποίηση λεξιλογίου, η αφαίρεση περιττών λέξεων και ο διαχωρισμός προτάσεων λειτουργούν εκτός σύνδεσης και δεν κοστίζουν τίποτα. Χρησιμοποιήστε τα ως εναλλακτική λύση όταν τα LLM API δεν λειτουργούν.
  • Τα πρότυπα prompt είναι το ανταγωνιστικό σας πλεονέκτημα: Το ίδιο LLM API είναι διαθέσιμο σε όλους. Τα προσεκτικά σχεδιασμένα πρότυπα prompt σας — με μηνύματα συστήματος, οδηγίες και περιορισμούς — καθορίζουν την ποιότητα και τη συνέπεια.
  • Το streaming είναι υποχρεωτικό για προϊόντα κειμένου: Οι χρήστες δεν θα περιμένουν 5–10 δευτερόλεπτα κοιτάζοντας έναν spinner. Το streaming λέξη-λέξη μέσω SSE κάνει το προϊόν να φαίνεται στιγμιαίο και ελκυστικό.
  • Διαχωρίστε τις αρμοδιότητες καθαρά: Analyzer, Transformer, PromptEngine και Streamer είναι ανεξάρτητα modules. Το καθένα μπορεί να δοκιμαστεί, να αντικατασταθεί ή να αναβαθμιστεί χωρίς να επηρεάσει τα υπόλοιπα.

Επόμενο: Στο GenAI-4, κατασκευάζετε ένα SaaS Παραγωγής Κώδικα — με διαχείριση μετασχηματισμών ευαίσθητων στη σύνταξη, υποστήριξη πολλαπλών γλωσσών και ασφαλή sandboxes εκτέλεσης κώδικα.
