Teil 1: Text-Analyse-Engine

Bevor du Text umschreibst, musst du ihn verstehen. Die Analyse-Engine bewertet die Lesbarkeit mit der Formel Flesch Reading Ease (0 = sehr schwer, 100 = sehr leicht), misst die Satzkomplexität und erkennt Muster in der Worthäufigkeit. Diese Kennzahlen steuern die Transformations-Pipeline und liefern den Nutzern einen “Vorher-Nachher”-Vergleich.

Python 

# analyzer.py - Text analysis engine for ProseAI

import re
from collections import Counter

class TextAnalyzer:
    """Analyze text for readability, complexity, and word frequency."""

    def count_syllables(self, word):
        """Estimate syllable count using vowel-group heuristic."""
        word = word.lower().strip()
        if len(word) == 0:
            return 0
        if word.endswith("e") and len(word) > 2:
            word = word[:-1]
        vowels = "aeiou"
        count = 0
        prev_vowel = False
        for ch in word:
            is_vowel = ch in vowels
            if is_vowel and not prev_vowel:
                count += 1
            prev_vowel = is_vowel
        return max(count, 1)

    def split_sentences(self, text):
        sentences = re.split(r"[.!?]+", text)
        return [s.strip() for s in sentences if s.strip()]

    def get_words(self, text):
        return re.findall(r"[a-zA-Z]+", text.lower())

    def flesch_reading_ease(self, text):
        """Flesch Reading Ease: 90-100 very easy, 0-30 very hard."""
        sentences = self.split_sentences(text)
        words = self.get_words(text)
        if not sentences or not words:
            return 0.0
        total_syl = sum(self.count_syllables(w) for w in words)
        asl = len(words) / len(sentences)
        asw = total_syl / len(words)
        score = 206.835 - (1.015 * asl) - (84.6 * asw)
        return round(max(0, min(100, score)), 1)

    def analyze(self, text):
        """Full text analysis: readability, complexity, frequency."""
        sentences = self.split_sentences(text)
        words = self.get_words(text)
        if not words:
            return {"error": "No text to analyze"}
        syl_counts = [self.count_syllables(w) for w in words]
        freq = Counter(words)
        complex_words = [w for w, s in zip(words, syl_counts) if s >= 3]
        avg_sl = len(words) / max(len(sentences), 1)
        avg_syl = sum(syl_counts) / len(words)
        grade = 0.39 * avg_sl + 11.8 * avg_syl - 15.59
        return {
            "word_count": len(words),
            "sentence_count": len(sentences),
            "avg_sentence_length": round(avg_sl, 1),
            "flesch_reading_ease": self.flesch_reading_ease(text),
            "grade_level": round(max(0, grade), 1),
            "vocabulary_richness": round(len(set(words)) / len(words), 3),
            "complex_word_pct": round(len(complex_words) / len(words) * 100, 1),
            "top_words": freq.most_common(5),
        }

    def reading_level_label(self, score):
        if score >= 80: return "Easy (6th grade or below)"
        elif score >= 60: return "Standard (8th-9th grade)"
        elif score >= 40: return "Difficult (10th-12th grade)"
        else: return "Very Difficult (College+)"

}

Teil 2: Text-Transformations-Pipeline

Die Transformations-Pipeline führt regelbasierte Textverarbeitung durch — Vereinfachung, Satztrennung und Entfernen von Füllwörtern — ganz ohne LLM. Das ist nützlich als Fallback, wenn APIs ausfallen, für leichtgewichtige Anfragen und als Vorverarbeitung vor dem LLM-basierten Umschreiben.

Python 

# transformer.py - Rule-based text transformation pipeline

import re

class TextTransformer:
    """Rule-based text transformations without LLM dependency."""

    SIMPLIFY_MAP = {
        "utilize": "use", "implement": "set up",
        "facilitate": "help", "subsequently": "then",
        "approximately": "about", "demonstrate": "show",
        "consequently": "so", "nevertheless": "still",
        "furthermore": "also", "comprehensive": "full",
        "fundamental": "basic", "methodology": "method",
        "sufficient": "enough", "necessitate": "need",
        "endeavor": "try", "commence": "start",
        "terminate": "end", "modifications": "changes",
        "functionality": "features",
    }

    FILLER_WORDS = [
        "very", "really", "basically", "actually", "literally",
        "definitely", "certainly", "absolutely", "simply",
        "quite", "rather", "somewhat", "just",
    ]

    def simplify_vocabulary(self, text):
        """Replace complex words with simpler alternatives."""
        result = text
        replacements = []
        for cw, sw in self.SIMPLIFY_MAP.items():
            pattern = re.compile(r"\\b" + cw + r"\\b", re.IGNORECASE)
            if pattern.search(result):
                def repl(m, simple=sw):
                    return simple.capitalize() if m.group(0)[0].isupper() else simple
                result = pattern.sub(repl, result)
                replacements.append(f"{cw} -> {sw}")
        return result, replacements

    def remove_fillers(self, text):
        """Remove filler words and unnecessary adverbs."""
        removed = []
        result = text
        for filler in self.FILLER_WORDS:
            pattern = re.compile(r"\\b" + filler + r"\\b\\s*", re.IGNORECASE)
            if pattern.search(result):
                result = pattern.sub("", result)
                removed.append(filler)
        return re.sub(r"\\s{2,}", " ", result).strip(), removed

    def split_long_sentences(self, text, max_words=25):
        """Break long sentences at conjunctions."""
        conjunctions = [", and ", ", but ", ", which ", "; ", ", however "]
        sentences = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\\s+", text)
        result = []
        for sentence in sentences:
            if len(sentence.split()) > max_words:
                split_done = False
                for conj in conjunctions:
                    if conj in sentence:
                        parts = sentence.split(conj, 1)
                        if len(parts[0].split()) >= 5:
                            result.append(parts[0].strip() + ".")
                            second = parts[1].strip()
                            if second and second[0].islower():
                                second = second[0].upper() + second[1:]
                            result.append(second)
                            split_done = True
                            break
                if not split_done:
                    result.append(sentence)
            else:
                result.append(sentence)
        return " ".join(result)

    def make_concise(self, text):
        """Apply all simplification rules."""
        text, vocab_changes = self.simplify_vocabulary(text)
        text, fillers_removed = self.remove_fillers(text)
        text = self.split_long_sentences(text)
        return {"text": text, "vocab_changes": vocab_changes,
                "fillers_removed": fillers_removed}

Teil 3: Prompt-Templates für LLM-basiertes Umschreiben

Die eigentliche Stärke von ProseAI kommt vom LLM-basierten Umschreiben. Jeder Modus (zusammenfassen, formell, locker, erweitern, vereinfachen) hat ein sorgfältig ausgearbeitetes Prompt-Template. Das Template-System trennt die System-Nachricht (Persona) von der Anweisung (Aufgabe) und dem Nutzerinhalt (zu transformierender Text). Gute Prompt-Templates sind dein Wettbewerbsvorteil — dieselbe LLM-API steht allen zur Verfügung, aber deine Templates entscheiden über die Qualität.

Python 

# prompts.py - Prompt template system for ProseAI

class PromptTemplateEngine:
    """Manages prompt templates for different rewriting modes."""

    TEMPLATES = {
        "summarize": {
            "name": "Summarize",
            "description": "Condense text to key points",
            "system": ("You are an expert summarizer. Extract the core meaning "
                       "and key points. Preserve factual accuracy."),
            "instruction": ("Summarize the following text in {length} sentences. "
                            "Keep the most important facts and conclusions."),
            "defaults": {"length": "2-3"},
        },
        "formal": {
            "name": "Formal Tone",
            "description": "Rewrite in professional, formal style",
            "system": ("You are a professional editor specializing in formal "
                       "business and academic writing."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text in a formal, professional tone. "
                            "Use precise vocabulary, avoid contractions. "
                            "Preserve all factual content."),
            "defaults": {},
        },
        "casual": {
            "name": "Casual Tone",
            "description": "Rewrite in friendly, conversational style",
            "system": ("You are a friendly writer who makes complex topics "
                       "accessible and conversational."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text in a casual, friendly tone. "
                            "Use everyday language. Do not lose any key information."),
            "defaults": {},
        },
        "expand": {
            "name": "Expand",
            "description": "Elaborate with more detail and examples",
            "system": ("You are a thorough writer who enriches content with "
                       "relevant details and examples."),
            "instruction": ("Expand the following text to approximately {target_length}. "
                            "Add relevant details and examples. "
                            "Do not add speculative information."),
            "defaults": {"target_length": "twice the original length"},
        },
        "simplify": {
            "name": "Simplify",
            "description": "Rewrite for easy reading (grade 6 level)",
            "system": ("You are a plain-language expert. Rewrite text so that "
                       "a 12-year-old can understand it."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text at a {grade} reading level. "
                            "Use short sentences (under 15 words). "
                            "Replace jargon with simple words."),
            "defaults": {"grade": "6th grade"},
        },
    }

    def build_prompt(self, mode, user_text, **kwargs):
        """Build a complete prompt for the given rewriting mode."""
        if mode not in self.TEMPLATES:
            return {"error": f"Unknown mode: {mode}"}
        t = self.TEMPLATES[mode]
        params = dict(t["defaults"])
        params.update(kwargs)
        instruction = t["instruction"].format(**params)
        return {
            "mode": mode, "mode_name": t["name"],
            "messages": [
                {"role": "system", "content": t["system"]},
                {"role": "user", "content": f"{instruction}\
\
---\
\
{user_text}"},
            ],
        }

    def list_modes(self):
        return {k: {"name": t["name"], "description": t["description"],
                     "params": list(t["defaults"].keys())}
                for k, t in self.TEMPLATES.items()}

Teil 4: Streaming-Antworten

Nutzer erwarten, dass Text Wort für Wort erscheint, wie bei ChatGPT. Streaming verbessert die gefühlte Latenz drastisch — statt 5 Sekunden auf eine vollständige Antwort zu warten, sehen Nutzer das erste Wort in unter 200 ms. ProseAI nutzt Python-Generatoren und Server-Sent Events (SSE), um umgeschriebenen Text in Echtzeit an das Frontend zu streamen.

Python 

# streaming.py - Streaming response generator for ProseAI

import json
import re

class StreamingRewriter:
    """Streaming text generation using the generator pattern.
    In production, this wraps the LLM API streaming response."""

    def sse_format(self, data):
        """Format data as a Server-Sent Event string."""
        return f"data: {json.dumps(data)}\
\
"

    def stream_rewrite(self, original, rewritten, mode):
        """Full streaming pipeline: start, tokens, done."""
        # 1. Start event
        yield self.sse_format({
            "type": "start", "mode": mode,
            "original_length": len(original.split()),
        })
        # 2. Stream word by word
        words = rewritten.split()
        for i, word in enumerate(words):
            yield self.sse_format({
                "type": "token", "content": word + " ", "index": i,
            })
        # 3. Done event with statistics
        yield self.sse_format({
            "type": "done",
            "original_words": len(original.split()),
            "rewritten_words": len(words),
            "compression": round(len(words) / max(len(original.split()), 1), 2),
        })


# --- Demo ---
streamer = StreamingRewriter()

original = (
    "The implementation of machine learning algorithms in production "
    "environments necessitates careful consideration of computational "
    "resources, data pipeline architecture, and model versioning."
)
rewritten = (
    "Putting ML models into production means thinking about three things. "
    "First, you need enough computing power. Second, your data pipelines "
    "must be solid. Third, keep track of your model versions."
)

events = list(streamer.stream_rewrite(original, rewritten, "simplify"))
print(f"Total SSE events: {len(events)}")

# Parse and display
output = ""
for event_str in events:
    data = json.loads(event_str.replace("data: ", "").strip())
    if data["type"] == "start":
        print(f"[START] Mode: {data['mode']}, Input: {data['original_length']} words")
    elif data["type"] == "token":
        output += data["content"]
    elif data["type"] == "done":
        print(f"[OUTPUT] {output.strip()}")
        print(f"[DONE] {data['original_words']} -> {data['rewritten_words']} words "
              f"({data['compression']}x)")

print(f"\
Sample SSE event:\
  {events[2].strip()}")

Teil 5: Der FastAPI-Server

Dies ist das Herzstück von ProseAI — der API-Server, der Analyse, Transformation, Prompt-Templates und Streaming zusammenführt. Der Endpunkt /api/rewrite unterstützt sowohl reguläre JSON-Antworten als auch SSE-Streaming über StreamingResponse.

app/main.py
"""ProseAI API Server - Text Composition and Rewriting SaaS."""
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Depends, Header
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
import uuid, time, asyncio

from .config import settings
from .analyzer import TextAnalyzer
from .transformer import TextTransformer
from .prompts import PromptTemplateEngine
from .streaming import StreamingRewriter

app = FastAPI(title="ProseAI API", version="1.0.0")
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory="static"), name="static")

analyzer = TextAnalyzer()
transformer = TextTransformer()
prompt_engine = PromptTemplateEngine()
streamer = StreamingRewriter()

class RewriteRequest(BaseModel):
    text: str = Field(..., min_length=10, max_length=10000)
    mode: str = Field(default="simplify")
    stream: bool = Field(default=False)
    params: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)

class AnalyzeRequest(BaseModel):
    text: str = Field(..., min_length=10, max_length=10000)

async def get_user(x_api_key: str = Header(...)):
    if not x_api_key:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="API key required")
    return {"id": "user_1", "tier": "pro"}

@app.get("/api/modes")
async def list_modes():
    return {"modes": prompt_engine.list_modes()}

@app.post("/api/analyze")
async def analyze_text(req: AnalyzeRequest):
    result = analyzer.analyze(req.text)
    result["reading_level"] = analyzer.reading_level_label(
        result["flesch_reading_ease"])
    return result

@app.post("/api/rewrite")
async def rewrite_text(req: RewriteRequest, user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Rewrite text in the specified mode. Supports streaming via SSE."""
    prompt_data = prompt_engine.build_prompt(req.mode, req.text, **req.params)
    if "error" in prompt_data:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=prompt_data["error"])

    if req.stream:
        async def event_generator():
            # In production: stream from LLM API using prompt_data
            result = transformer.make_concise(req.text)
            for event in streamer.stream_rewrite(
                    req.text, result["text"], req.mode):
                yield event
                await asyncio.sleep(0.02)
        return StreamingResponse(event_generator(),
            media_type="text/event-stream",
            headers={"Cache-Control": "no-cache", "X-Accel-Buffering": "no"})

    # Non-streaming: return complete JSON response
    start = time.time()
    result = transformer.make_concise(req.text)
    return {
        "id": str(uuid.uuid4()), "mode": req.mode,
        "rewritten_text": result["text"],
        "analysis_before": analyzer.analyze(req.text),
        "analysis_after": analyzer.analyze(result["text"]),
        "processing_time": round(time.time() - start, 3),
    }

@app.get("/api/health")
async def health():
    return {"status": "ok", "service": "proseai"}

Teil 11: Verbindung zu deinem eigenen LLM

Bisher haben wir APIs von Drittanbietern verwendet. Die eigentliche Stärke — und die eigentlichen Margen — entstehen aber, wenn du deine eigenen Modelle betreibst. Das eliminiert API-Kosten pro Anfrage, gibt dir volle Kontrolle über Latenz und Datenschutz und erlaubt dir, Modelle für deinen konkreten Anwendungsfall feinabzustimmen.

Drei Hauptansätze für Self-Hosting:

  • vLLM — höchster Durchsatz, OpenAI-kompatible API, am besten für Produktion
  • Ollama — einfachste Einrichtung, hervorragend für Entwicklung und kleine Deployments
  • llama.cpp — geringster Ressourcenbedarf, läuft auf der CPU, ideal für Edge-Deployment

Für Textgenerierung self-hosten mit vLLM, llama.cpp oder Ollama:

Teil 13: Rate Limiting & API-Schutz

Jedes produktive SaaS braucht Rate Limiting, um Missbrauch zu verhindern, Kosten zu kontrollieren und eine faire Nutzung sicherzustellen. Hier ist eine produktionsreife Implementierung:

rate_limiter.py — Production Rate Limiting for ProseAI
"""
Production rate limiting for ProseAI.
Three tiers: in-memory (development), Redis (production), token bucket (advanced).
"""
import time
from collections import defaultdict

# === TIER 1: In-Memory Rate Limiter (Development) ===
class InMemoryRateLimiter:
    """Simple sliding window rate limiter. Works for single-server setup."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.requests = defaultdict(list)

    def is_allowed(self, key, max_requests, window_seconds):
        """Check if request is allowed under the rate limit."""
        now = time.time()
        window_start = now - window_seconds

        # Clean old entries
        self.requests[key] = [t for t in self.requests[key] if t > window_start]

        if len(self.requests[key]) >= max_requests:
            retry_after = self.requests[key][0] - window_start
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "limit": max_requests,
                "window": window_seconds,
                "retry_after": round(retry_after, 1),
                "current": len(self.requests[key])
            }}

        self.requests[key].append(now)
        return True, {{
            "remaining": max_requests - len(self.requests[key]),
            "limit": max_requests,
            "reset": round(window_start + window_seconds - now, 1)
        }}

# === TIER 2: Redis Rate Limiter (Production) ===
class RedisRateLimiter:
    """Redis-based rate limiter for distributed deployments.

    In production, install: pip install redis
    And use a real Redis connection.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        # In production: self.redis = redis.Redis(host='redis', port=6379, db=0)
        self.memory = defaultdict(list)  # Simulating Redis

    def check_rate_limit(self, user_id, tier="free"):
        """Check rate limit based on user tier."""
        limits = {{
            "free":       {{"requests_per_minute": 5,  "requests_per_day": 50}},
            "starter":    {{"requests_per_minute": 20, "requests_per_day": 500}},
            "pro":        {{"requests_per_minute": 60, "requests_per_day": 5000}},
            "enterprise": {{"requests_per_minute": 200, "requests_per_day": 50000}},
        }}

        tier_limits = limits.get(tier, limits["free"])
        now = time.time()

        # Check per-minute limit
        minute_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:minute"
        self.memory[minute_key] = [t for t in self.memory[minute_key] if t > now - 60]

        if len(self.memory[minute_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_minute"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_minute",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"],
                "retry_after_seconds": 60 - (now - self.memory[minute_key][0])
            }}

        # Check per-day limit
        day_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:day"
        self.memory[day_key] = [t for t in self.memory[day_key] if t > now - 86400]

        if len(self.memory[day_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_day"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "daily_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_day",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_day"],
            }}

        # Allow request
        self.memory[minute_key].append(now)
        self.memory[day_key].append(now)

        return True, {{
            "remaining_minute": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"] - len(self.memory[minute_key]),
            "remaining_day": tier_limits["requests_per_day"] - len(self.memory[day_key]),
        }}

# === FastAPI Middleware ===
class RateLimitMiddleware:
    """
    FastAPI middleware for rate limiting.

    Usage in your app:
        from rate_limiter import RateLimitMiddleware
        app.add_middleware(RateLimitMiddleware)

    Or as a dependency:
        @app.get("/generate")
        async def generate(rate_limit: dict = Depends(check_rate_limit)):
            ...
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.limiter = RedisRateLimiter()

    def get_middleware_code(self):
        """Print the actual FastAPI middleware code."""
        code = "# Add to your FastAPI app:\
\
"
        code += "from fastapi import Request, Response\
"
        code += "from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware\
\
"
        code += "class RateLimitMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):\
"
        code += "    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):\
"
        code += "        api_key = request.headers.get('X-API-Key', 'anonymous')\
"
        code += "        user_id = self.get_user_from_key(api_key)\
"
        code += "        tier = self.get_user_tier(user_id)\
"
        code += "        allowed, info = self.limiter.check_rate_limit(user_id, tier)\
"
        code += "        if not allowed:\
"
        code += "            return JSONResponse(status_code=429, content=info)\
"
        code += "        response = await call_next(request)\
"
        code += "        response.headers['X-RateLimit-Remaining'] = str(info.get('remaining_minute', 0))\
"
        code += "        return response\
"
        print(code)

Wichtigste Erkenntnisse

  • Analysiere, bevor du transformierst: Das Messen von Lesbarkeit, Satzkomplexität und Worthäufigkeit liefert dir objektive Kennzahlen. So kannst du Nutzern einen “Vorher-Nachher”-Vergleich zeigen, der den Mehrwert deines Dienstes belegt.
  • Regelbasierte Transformationen sind dein Sicherheitsnetz: Vokabelvereinfachung, Entfernen von Füllwörtern und Satztrennung funktionieren offline und kosten nichts. Nutze sie als Fallback, wenn LLM-APIs ausfallen.
  • Prompt-Templates sind dein Burggraben: Dieselbe LLM-API steht allen zur Verfügung. Deine sorgfältig ausgearbeiteten Prompt-Templates — mit System-Nachrichten, Anweisungen und Einschränkungen — entscheiden über Qualität und Konsistenz.
  • Streaming ist bei Textprodukten Pflicht: Nutzer warten nicht 5–10 Sekunden vor einem Ladesymbol. Wort-für-Wort-Streaming über SSE lässt das Produkt sofort reaktionsfähig und ansprechend wirken.
  • Trenne Zuständigkeiten sauber: Analyzer, Transformer, PromptEngine und Streamer sind unabhängige Module. Jedes kann getestet, ersetzt oder aktualisiert werden, ohne die anderen zu berühren.

Als Nächstes: In GenAI-4 baust du ein SaaS zur Codegenerierung — mit syntaxbewussten Transformationen, Unterstützung mehrerer Sprachen und sicheren Sandboxes zur Codeausführung.

Partie 1 : Le moteur d'analyse de texte

Avant de réécrire un texte, vous devez le comprendre. Le moteur d'analyse évalue la lisibilité à l'aide de la formule Flesch Reading Ease (0 = très difficile, 100 = très facile), mesure la complexité des phrases et identifie les tendances de fréquence des mots. Ces métriques guident le pipeline de transformation et offrent aux utilisateurs une comparaison “avant vs. après”.

Python 

# analyzer.py - Text analysis engine for ProseAI

import re
from collections import Counter

class TextAnalyzer:
    """Analyze text for readability, complexity, and word frequency."""

    def count_syllables(self, word):
        """Estimate syllable count using vowel-group heuristic."""
        word = word.lower().strip()
        if len(word) == 0:
            return 0
        if word.endswith("e") and len(word) > 2:
            word = word[:-1]
        vowels = "aeiou"
        count = 0
        prev_vowel = False
        for ch in word:
            is_vowel = ch in vowels
            if is_vowel and not prev_vowel:
                count += 1
            prev_vowel = is_vowel
        return max(count, 1)

    def split_sentences(self, text):
        sentences = re.split(r"[.!?]+", text)
        return [s.strip() for s in sentences if s.strip()]

    def get_words(self, text):
        return re.findall(r"[a-zA-Z]+", text.lower())

    def flesch_reading_ease(self, text):
        """Flesch Reading Ease: 90-100 very easy, 0-30 very hard."""
        sentences = self.split_sentences(text)
        words = self.get_words(text)
        if not sentences or not words:
            return 0.0
        total_syl = sum(self.count_syllables(w) for w in words)
        asl = len(words) / len(sentences)
        asw = total_syl / len(words)
        score = 206.835 - (1.015 * asl) - (84.6 * asw)
        return round(max(0, min(100, score)), 1)

    def analyze(self, text):
        """Full text analysis: readability, complexity, frequency."""
        sentences = self.split_sentences(text)
        words = self.get_words(text)
        if not words:
            return {"error": "No text to analyze"}
        syl_counts = [self.count_syllables(w) for w in words]
        freq = Counter(words)
        complex_words = [w for w, s in zip(words, syl_counts) if s >= 3]
        avg_sl = len(words) / max(len(sentences), 1)
        avg_syl = sum(syl_counts) / len(words)
        grade = 0.39 * avg_sl + 11.8 * avg_syl - 15.59
        return {
            "word_count": len(words),
            "sentence_count": len(sentences),
            "avg_sentence_length": round(avg_sl, 1),
            "flesch_reading_ease": self.flesch_reading_ease(text),
            "grade_level": round(max(0, grade), 1),
            "vocabulary_richness": round(len(set(words)) / len(words), 3),
            "complex_word_pct": round(len(complex_words) / len(words) * 100, 1),
            "top_words": freq.most_common(5),
        }

    def reading_level_label(self, score):
        if score >= 80: return "Easy (6th grade or below)"
        elif score >= 60: return "Standard (8th-9th grade)"
        elif score >= 40: return "Difficult (10th-12th grade)"
        else: return "Very Difficult (College+)"


# --- Demo ---
analyzer = TextAnalyzer()

samples = {

    ),

    ),

        "architectures in contemporary technological paradigms."
    ),
}

for label, text in samples.items():
    r = analyzer.analyze(text)
    fre = r["flesch_reading_ease"]
    print(f"=== {label} Text ===")

Partie 2 : Le pipeline de transformation de texte

Le pipeline de transformation effectue un traitement de texte basé sur des règles — simplification, découpage des phrases et suppression des mots de remplissage — sans avoir besoin d'un LLM. Ceci est utile comme solution de repli lorsque les API sont indisponibles, pour les requêtes légères, et comme prétraitement avant la réécriture basée sur un LLM.

Python 

# transformer.py - Rule-based text transformation pipeline

import re

class TextTransformer:
    """Rule-based text transformations without LLM dependency."""

    SIMPLIFY_MAP = {
        "utilize": "use", "implement": "set up",
        "facilitate": "help", "subsequently": "then",
        "approximately": "about", "demonstrate": "show",
        "consequently": "so", "nevertheless": "still",
        "furthermore": "also", "comprehensive": "full",
        "fundamental": "basic", "methodology": "method",
        "sufficient": "enough", "necessitate": "need",
        "endeavor": "try", "commence": "start",
        "terminate": "end", "modifications": "changes",
        "functionality": "features",
    }

    FILLER_WORDS = [
        "very", "really", "basically", "actually", "literally",
        "definitely", "certainly", "absolutely", "simply",
        "quite", "rather", "somewhat", "just",
    ]

    def simplify_vocabulary(self, text):
        """Replace complex words with simpler alternatives."""
        result = text
        replacements = []
        for cw, sw in self.SIMPLIFY_MAP.items():
            pattern = re.compile(r"\\b" + cw + r"\\b", re.IGNORECASE)
            if pattern.search(result):
                def repl(m, simple=sw):
                    return simple.capitalize() if m.group(0)[0].isupper() else simple
                result = pattern.sub(repl, result)
                replacements.append(f"{cw} -> {sw}")
        return result, replacements

    def remove_fillers(self, text):
        """Remove filler words and unnecessary adverbs."""
        removed = []
        result = text
        for filler in self.FILLER_WORDS:
            pattern = re.compile(r"\\b" + filler + r"\\b\\s*", re.IGNORECASE)
            if pattern.search(result):
                result = pattern.sub("", result)
                removed.append(filler)
        return re.sub(r"\\s{2,}", " ", result).strip(), removed

    def split_long_sentences(self, text, max_words=25):
        """Break long sentences at conjunctions."""
        conjunctions = [", and ", ", but ", ", which ", "; ", ", however "]
        sentences = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\\s+", text)
        result = []
        for sentence in sentences:
            if len(sentence.split()) > max_words:
                split_done = False
                for conj in conjunctions:
                    if conj in sentence:
                        parts = sentence.split(conj, 1)
                        if len(parts[0].split()) >= 5:
                            result.append(parts[0].strip() + ".")
                            second = parts[1].strip()
                            if second and second[0].islower():
                                second = second[0].upper() + second[1:]
                            result.append(second)
                            split_done = True
                            break
                if not split_done:
                    result.append(sentence)
            else:
                result.append(sentence)
        return " ".join(result)

    def make_concise(self, text):
        """Apply all simplification rules."""
        text, vocab_changes = self.simplify_vocabulary(text)
        text, fillers_removed = self.remove_fillers(text)
        text = self.split_long_sentences(text)
        return {"text": text, "vocab_changes": vocab_changes,
                "fillers_removed": fillers_removed}


# --- Demo ---
transformer = TextTransformer()

)

=== After All Transforms ===")

Partie 3 : Modèles de prompt pour la réécriture basée sur un LLM

La véritable puissance de ProseAI vient de la réécriture basée sur un LLM. Chaque mode (résumer, formel, familier, développer, simplifier) dispose d'un modèle de prompt soigneusement conçu. Le système de modèles sépare le message système (persona) de l'instruction (tâche) et du contenu utilisateur (texte à transformer). De bons modèles de prompt constituent votre avantage concurrentiel — la même API LLM est disponible pour tout le monde, mais ce sont vos modèles qui déterminent la qualité.

Python 

# prompts.py - Prompt template system for ProseAI

class PromptTemplateEngine:
    """Manages prompt templates for different rewriting modes."""

    TEMPLATES = {
        "summarize": {
            "name": "Summarize",
            "description": "Condense text to key points",
            "system": ("You are an expert summarizer. Extract the core meaning "
                       "and key points. Preserve factual accuracy."),
            "instruction": ("Summarize the following text in {length} sentences. "
                            "Keep the most important facts and conclusions."),
            "defaults": {"length": "2-3"},
        },
        "formal": {
            "name": "Formal Tone",
            "description": "Rewrite in professional, formal style",
            "system": ("You are a professional editor specializing in formal "
                       "business and academic writing."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text in a formal, professional tone. "
                            "Use precise vocabulary, avoid contractions. "
                            "Preserve all factual content."),
            "defaults": {},
        },
        "casual": {
            "name": "Casual Tone",
            "description": "Rewrite in friendly, conversational style",
            "system": ("You are a friendly writer who makes complex topics "
                       "accessible and conversational."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text in a casual, friendly tone. "
                            "Use everyday language. Do not lose any key information."),
            "defaults": {},
        },
        "expand": {
            "name": "Expand",
            "description": "Elaborate with more detail and examples",
            "system": ("You are a thorough writer who enriches content with "
                       "relevant details and examples."),
            "instruction": ("Expand the following text to approximately {target_length}. "
                            "Add relevant details and examples. "
                            "Do not add speculative information."),
            "defaults": {"target_length": "twice the original length"},
        },
        "simplify": {
            "name": "Simplify",
            "description": "Rewrite for easy reading (grade 6 level)",
            "system": ("You are a plain-language expert. Rewrite text so that "
                       "a 12-year-old can understand it."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text at a {grade} reading level. "
                            "Use short sentences (under 15 words). "
                            "Replace jargon with simple words."),
            "defaults": {"grade": "6th grade"},
        },
    }

    def build_prompt(self, mode, user_text, **kwargs):
        """Build a complete prompt for the given rewriting mode."""
        if mode not in self.TEMPLATES:
            return {"error": f"Unknown mode: {mode}"}
        t = self.TEMPLATES[mode]
        params = dict(t["defaults"])
        params.update(kwargs)
        instruction = t["instruction"].format(**params)
        return {
            "mode": mode, "mode_name": t["name"],
            "messages": [
                {"role": "system", "content": t["system"]},
                {"role": "user", "content": f"{instruction}\
\
---\
\
{user_text}"},
            ],
        }

    def list_modes(self):
        return {k: {"name": t["name"], "description": t["description"],
                     "params": list(t["defaults"].keys())}
                for k, t in self.TEMPLATES.items()}


# --- Demo ---

Partie 4 : Réponses en streaming

Les utilisateurs s'attendent à voir le texte apparaître mot par mot, comme avec ChatGPT. Le streaming améliore considérablement la latence perçue — au lieu d'attendre 5 secondes pour une réponse complète, les utilisateurs voient le premier mot en moins de 200 ms. ProseAI utilise des générateurs Python et les Server-Sent Events (SSE) pour diffuser le texte réécrit vers le frontend en temps réel.

Python 

# streaming.py - Streaming response generator for ProseAI

import json
import re

class StreamingRewriter:
    """Streaming text generation using the generator pattern.
    In production, this wraps the LLM API streaming response."""

    def sse_format(self, data):
        """Format data as a Server-Sent Event string."""
        return f"data: {json.dumps(data)}\
\
"

    def stream_rewrite(self, original, rewritten, mode):
        """Full streaming pipeline: start, tokens, done."""
        # 1. Start event
        yield self.sse_format({
            "type": "start", "mode": mode,
            "original_length": len(original.split()),
        })
        # 2. Stream word by word
        words = rewritten.split()
        for i, word in enumerate(words):
            yield self.sse_format({
                "type": "token", "content": word + " ", "index": i,
            })
        # 3. Done event with statistics
        yield self.sse_format({
            "type": "done",
            "original_words": len(original.split()),
            "rewritten_words": len(words),
            "compression": round(len(words) / max(len(original.split()), 1), 2),
        })


# --- Demo ---
streamer = StreamingRewriter()

original = (
    "The implementation of machine learning algorithms in production "
    "environments necessitates careful consideration of computational "
    "resources, data pipeline architecture, and model versioning."
)
rewritten = (
    "Putting ML models into production means thinking about three things. "
    "First, you need enough computing power. Second, your data pipelines "
    "must be solid. Third, keep track of your model versions."
)

events = list(streamer.stream_rewrite(original, rewritten, "simplify"))
print(f"Total SSE events: {len(events)}")

# Parse and display
output = ""
for event_str in events:
    data = json.loads(event_str.replace("data: ", "").strip())
    if data["type"] == "start":
        print(f"[START] Mode: {data['mode']}, Input: {data['original_length']} words")
    elif data["type"] == "token":
        output += data["content"]
    elif data["type"] == "done":
        print(f"[OUTPUT] {output.strip()}")
        print(f"[DONE] {data['original_words']} -> {data['rewritten_words']} words "
              f"({data['compression']}x)")

print(f"\
Sample SSE event:\
  {events[2].strip()}")

Partie 5 : Le serveur FastAPI

C'est le cœur de ProseAI — le serveur API qui relie l'analyse, la transformation, les modèles de prompt et le streaming. Le endpoint /api/rewrite prend en charge à la fois les réponses JSON classiques et le streaming SSE via StreamingResponse.

app/main.py
"""ProseAI API Server - Text Composition and Rewriting SaaS."""
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Depends, Header
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
import uuid, time, asyncio

from .config import settings
from .analyzer import TextAnalyzer
from .transformer import TextTransformer
from .prompts import PromptTemplateEngine
from .streaming import StreamingRewriter

app = FastAPI(title="ProseAI API", version="1.0.0")
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory="static"), name="static")

analyzer = TextAnalyzer()
transformer = TextTransformer()
prompt_engine = PromptTemplateEngine()
streamer = StreamingRewriter()

class RewriteRequest(BaseModel):
    text: str = Field(..., min_length=10, max_length=10000)
    mode: str = Field(default="simplify")
    stream: bool = Field(default=False)
    params: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)

class AnalyzeRequest(BaseModel):
    text: str = Field(..., min_length=10, max_length=10000)

async def get_user(x_api_key: str = Header(...)):
    if not x_api_key:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="API key required")
    return {"id": "user_1", "tier": "pro"}

@app.get("/api/modes")
async def list_modes():
    return {"modes": prompt_engine.list_modes()}

@app.post("/api/analyze")
async def analyze_text(req: AnalyzeRequest):
    result = analyzer.analyze(req.text)
    result["reading_level"] = analyzer.reading_level_label(
        result["flesch_reading_ease"])
    return result

@app.post("/api/rewrite")
async def rewrite_text(req: RewriteRequest, user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Rewrite text in the specified mode. Supports streaming via SSE."""
    prompt_data = prompt_engine.build_prompt(req.mode, req.text, **req.params)
    if "error" in prompt_data:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=prompt_data["error"])

    if req.stream:
        async def event_generator():
            # In production: stream from LLM API using prompt_data
            result = transformer.make_concise(req.text)
            for event in streamer.stream_rewrite(
                    req.text, result["text"], req.mode):
                yield event
                await asyncio.sleep(0.02)
        return StreamingResponse(event_generator(),
            media_type="text/event-stream",
            headers={"Cache-Control": "no-cache", "X-Accel-Buffering": "no"})

    # Non-streaming: return complete JSON response
    start = time.time()
    result = transformer.make_concise(req.text)
    return {
        "id": str(uuid.uuid4()), "mode": req.mode,
        "rewritten_text": result["text"],
        "analysis_before": analyzer.analyze(req.text),
        "analysis_after": analyzer.analyze(result["text"]),
        "processing_time": round(time.time() - start, 3),
    }

Partie 11 : Connectez-vous à votre propre LLM

Jusqu'à présent, nous avons utilisé des API tierces. Mais la véritable puissance — et les véritables marges — apparaissent lorsque vous exécutez vos propres modèles. Cela élimine les coûts d'API par requête, vous donne un contrôle total sur la latence et la confidentialité, et vous permet d'affiner des modèles pour votre cas d'usage spécifique.

Trois approches principales pour l'auto-hébergement :

  • vLLM — débit le plus élevé, API compatible OpenAI, idéal pour la production
  • Ollama — configuration la plus simple, idéal pour le développement et les déploiements à petite échelle
  • llama.cpp — le plus léger, fonctionne sur CPU, idéal pour le déploiement en edge

Pour la génération de texte, auto-hébergez avec vLLM, llama.cpp, ou Ollama :

Partie 13 : Limitation de débit et protection de l'API

Chaque SaaS en production a besoin d'une limitation de débit pour prévenir les abus, maîtriser les coûts et garantir une utilisation équitable. Voici une implémentation de qualité production :

rate_limiter.py — Production Rate Limiting for ProseAI
"""
Production rate limiting for ProseAI.
Three tiers: in-memory (development), Redis (production), token bucket (advanced).
"""
import time
from collections import defaultdict

# === TIER 1: In-Memory Rate Limiter (Development) ===
class InMemoryRateLimiter:
    """Simple sliding window rate limiter. Works for single-server setup."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.requests = defaultdict(list)

    def is_allowed(self, key, max_requests, window_seconds):
        """Check if request is allowed under the rate limit."""
        now = time.time()
        window_start = now - window_seconds

        # Clean old entries
        self.requests[key] = [t for t in self.requests[key] if t > window_start]

        if len(self.requests[key]) >= max_requests:
            retry_after = self.requests[key][0] - window_start
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "limit": max_requests,
                "window": window_seconds,
                "retry_after": round(retry_after, 1),
                "current": len(self.requests[key])
            }}

        self.requests[key].append(now)
        return True, {{
            "remaining": max_requests - len(self.requests[key]),
            "limit": max_requests,
            "reset": round(window_start + window_seconds - now, 1)
        }}

# === TIER 2: Redis Rate Limiter (Production) ===
class RedisRateLimiter:
    """Redis-based rate limiter for distributed deployments.

    In production, install: pip install redis
    And use a real Redis connection.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        # In production: self.redis = redis.Redis(host='redis', port=6379, db=0)
        self.memory = defaultdict(list)  # Simulating Redis

    def check_rate_limit(self, user_id, tier="free"):
        """Check rate limit based on user tier."""
        limits = {{
            "free":       {{"requests_per_minute": 5,  "requests_per_day": 50}},
            "starter":    {{"requests_per_minute": 20, "requests_per_day": 500}},
            "pro":        {{"requests_per_minute": 60, "requests_per_day": 5000}},
            "enterprise": {{"requests_per_minute": 200, "requests_per_day": 50000}},
        }}

        tier_limits = limits.get(tier, limits["free"])
        now = time.time()

        # Check per-minute limit
        minute_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:minute"
        self.memory[minute_key] = [t for t in self.memory[minute_key] if t > now - 60]

        if len(self.memory[minute_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_minute"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_minute",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"],
                "retry_after_seconds": 60 - (now - self.memory[minute_key][0])
            }}

        # Check per-day limit
        day_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:day"
        self.memory[day_key] = [t for t in self.memory[day_key] if t > now - 86400]

        if len(self.memory[day_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_day"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "daily_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_day",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_day"],
            }}

        # Allow request
        self.memory[minute_key].append(now)
        self.memory[day_key].append(now)

        return True, {{
            "remaining_minute": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"] - len(self.memory[minute_key]),
            "remaining_day": tier_limits["requests_per_day"] - len(self.memory[day_key]),
        }}

# === FastAPI Middleware ===
class RateLimitMiddleware:
    """
    FastAPI middleware for rate limiting.

    Usage in your app:
        from rate_limiter import RateLimitMiddleware
        app.add_middleware(RateLimitMiddleware)

    Or as a dependency:
        @app.get("/generate")
        async def generate(rate_limit: dict = Depends(check_rate_limit)):
            ...
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.limiter = RedisRateLimiter()

Points clés à retenir

  • Analysez avant de transformer : Mesurer la lisibilité, la complexité des phrases et la fréquence des mots vous donne des métriques objectives. Cela vous permet de montrer aux utilisateurs une comparaison “avant vs. après” qui prouve que votre service apporte de la valeur.
  • Les transformations basées sur des règles sont votre filet de sécurité : La simplification du vocabulaire, la suppression des mots de remplissage et le découpage des phrases fonctionnent hors ligne et ne coûtent rien. Utilisez-les comme solutions de repli lorsque les API LLM sont indisponibles.
  • Les modèles de prompt sont votre rempart concurrentiel : La même API LLM est disponible pour tout le monde. Vos modèles de prompt soigneusement conçus — avec messages système, instructions et contraintes — déterminent la qualité et la cohérence.
  • Le streaming est indispensable pour les produits textuels : Les utilisateurs n'attendront pas 5–10 secondes en fixant un indicateur de chargement. Le streaming mot par mot via SSE donne au produit une sensation d'instantanéité et d'engagement.
  • Séparez clairement les responsabilités : Analyzer, Transformer, PromptEngine et Streamer sont des modules indépendants. Chacun peut être testé, remplacé ou amélioré sans toucher aux autres.

Suite : Dans GenAI-4, vous construirez un SaaS de génération de code — gérant des transformations conscientes de la syntaxe, la prise en charge multi-langages et des sandboxes d'exécution de code sécurisés.

Parte 1: Motore di Analisi del Testo

Prima di riscrivere un testo, devi capirlo. Il motore di analisi valuta la leggibilità usando la formula Flesch Reading Ease (0 = molto difficile, 100 = molto facile), misura la complessità delle frasi e identifica gli schemi di frequenza delle parole. Queste metriche guidano la pipeline di trasformazione e offrono agli utenti un confronto “prima vs. dopo”.

Python 

# analyzer.py - Motore di analisi del testo per ProseAI

import re
from collections import Counter

class TextAnalyzer:
    """Analizza il testo per leggibilità, complessità e frequenza delle parole."""

    def count_syllables(self, word):
        """Stima il numero di sillabe usando un'euristica sui gruppi di vocali."""
        word = word.lower().strip()
        if len(word) == 0:
            return 0
        if word.endswith("e") and len(word) > 2:
            word = word[:-1]
        vowels = "aeiou"
        count = 0
        prev_vowel = False
        for ch in word:
            is_vowel = ch in vowels
            if is_vowel and not prev_vowel:
                count += 1
            prev_vowel = is_vowel
        return max(count, 1)

    def split_sentences(self, text):
        sentences = re.split(r"[.!?]+", text)
        return [s.strip() for s in sentences if s.strip()]

    def get_words(self, text):
        return re.findall(r"[a-zA-Z]+", text.lower())

    def flesch_reading_ease(self, text):
        """Flesch Reading Ease: 90-100 molto facile, 0-30 molto difficile."""
        sentences = self.split_sentences(text)
        words = self.get_words(text)
        if not sentences or not words:
            return 0.0
        total_syl = sum(self.count_syllables(w) for w in words)
        asl = len(words) / len(sentences)
        asw = total_syl / len(words)
        score = 206.835 - (1.015 * asl) - (84.6 * asw)
        return round(max(0, min(100, score)), 1)

    def analyze(self, text):
        """Analisi completa del testo: leggibilità, complessità, frequenza."""
        sentences = self.split_sentences(text)
        words = self.get_words(text)
        if not words:
            return {"error": "Nessun testo da analizzare"}
        syl_counts = [self.count_syllables(w) for w in words]
        freq = Counter(words)
        complex_words = [w for w, s in zip(words, syl_counts) if s >= 3]
        avg_sl = len(words) / max(len(sentences), 1)
        avg_syl = sum(syl_counts) / len(words)
        grade = 0.39 * avg_sl + 11.8 * avg_syl - 15.59
        return {
            "word_count": len(words),
            "sentence_count": len(sentences),
            "avg_sentence_length": round(avg_sl, 1),
            "flesch_reading_ease": self.flesch_reading_ease(text),
            "grade_level": round(max(0, grade), 1),
            "vocabulary_richness": round(len(set(words)) / len(words), 3),
            "complex_word_pct": round(len(complex_words) / len(words) * 100, 1),
            "top_words": freq.most_common(5),
        }

    def reading_level_label(self, score):
        if score >= 80: return "Facile (6a elementare o inferiore)"
        elif score >= 60: return "Standard (2a-3a media)"
        elif score >= 40: return "Difficile (Superiori)"
        else: return "Molto Difficile (Universitario+)"


# --- Demo ---
analyzer = TextAnalyzer()

samples = {
    "Simple": (
        "The cat sat on the mat. It was a nice day. "
        "The sun was warm. Birds sang in the trees."
    ),
    "Medium": (
        "Machine learning algorithms process large datasets to identify "
        "patterns and make predictions. These systems improve their "
        "performance over time through experience."
    ),
    "Complex": (
        "The epistemological implications of artificial intelligence "
        "necessitate a fundamental reconceptualization of computational "
        "hermeneutics, particularly regarding the phenomenological "
        "intersection of algorithmic determinism and emergent cognitive "
        "architectures in contemporary technological paradigms."
    ),
}

for label, text in samples.items():
    r = analyzer.analyze(text)
    fre = r["flesch_reading_ease"]
    print(f"=== {label} Text ===")
    print(f"  Words: {r['word_count']}, Sentences: {r['sentence_count']}")
    print(f"  Avg sentence length: {r['avg_sentence_length']} words")
    print(f"  Flesch Reading Ease: {fre} ({analyzer.reading_level_label(fre)})")
    print(f"  Grade level: {r['grade_level']}")
    print(f"  Complex words: {r['complex_word_pct']}%")
    print()

Parte 2: Pipeline di Trasformazione del Testo

La pipeline di trasformazione esegue elaborazioni del testo basate su regole — semplificazione, suddivisione delle frasi e rimozione di parole di riempimento — senza bisogno di un LLM. È utile come fallback quando le API non sono disponibili, per richieste leggere e come pre-elaborazione prima della riscrittura basata su LLM.

Python 

# transformer.py - Pipeline di trasformazione del testo basata su regole

import re

class TextTransformer:
    """Trasformazioni del testo basate su regole, senza dipendenza da un LLM."""

    SIMPLIFY_MAP = {
        "utilize": "use", "implement": "set up",
        "facilitate": "help", "subsequently": "then",
        "approximately": "about", "demonstrate": "show",
        "consequently": "so", "nevertheless": "still",
        "furthermore": "also", "comprehensive": "full",
        "fundamental": "basic", "methodology": "method",
        "sufficient": "enough", "necessitate": "need",
        "endeavor": "try", "commence": "start",
        "terminate": "end", "modifications": "changes",
        "functionality": "features",
    }

    FILLER_WORDS = [
        "very", "really", "basically", "actually", "literally",
        "definitely", "certainly", "absolutely", "simply",
        "quite", "rather", "somewhat", "just",
    ]

    def simplify_vocabulary(self, text):
        """Sostituisce le parole complesse con alternative più semplici."""
        result = text
        replacements = []
        for cw, sw in self.SIMPLIFY_MAP.items():
            pattern = re.compile(r"\\b" + cw + r"\\b", re.IGNORECASE)
            if pattern.search(result):
                def repl(m, simple=sw):
                    return simple.capitalize() if m.group(0)[0].isupper() else simple
                result = pattern.sub(repl, result)
                replacements.append(f"{cw} -> {sw}")
        return result, replacements

    def remove_fillers(self, text):
        """Rimuove le parole di riempimento e gli avverbi non necessari."""
        removed = []
        result = text
        for filler in self.FILLER_WORDS:
            pattern = re.compile(r"\\b" + filler + r"\\b\\s*", re.IGNORECASE)
            if pattern.search(result):
                result = pattern.sub("", result)
                removed.append(filler)
        return re.sub(r"\\s{2,}", " ", result).strip(), removed

    def split_long_sentences(self, text, max_words=25):
        """Spezza le frasi lunghe in corrispondenza delle congiunzioni."""
        conjunctions = [", and ", ", but ", ", which ", "; ", ", however "]
        sentences = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\\s+", text)
        result = []
        for sentence in sentences:
            if len(sentence.split()) > max_words:
                split_done = False
                for conj in conjunctions:
                    if conj in sentence:
                        parts = sentence.split(conj, 1)
                        if len(parts[0].split()) >= 5:
                            result.append(parts[0].strip() + ".")
                            second = parts[1].strip()
                            if second and second[0].islower():
                                second = second[0].upper() + second[1:]
                            result.append(second)
                            split_done = True
                            break
                if not split_done:
                    result.append(sentence)
            else:
                result.append(sentence)
        return " ".join(result)

    def make_concise(self, text):
        """Applica tutte le regole di semplificazione."""
        text, vocab_changes = self.simplify_vocabulary(text)
        text, fillers_removed = self.remove_fillers(text)
        text = self.split_long_sentences(text)
        return {"text": text, "vocab_changes": vocab_changes,
                "fillers_removed": fillers_removed}

Parte 3: Template di Prompt per la Riscrittura Basata su LLM

La vera potenza di ProseAI viene dalla riscrittura basata su LLM. Ogni modalità (riassumi, formale, informale, espandi, semplifica) ha un template di prompt costruito con cura. Il sistema di template separa il messaggio di sistema (persona) dall'istruzione (compito) e dal contenuto dell'utente (testo da trasformare). I buoni template di prompt sono il tuo vantaggio competitivo — la stessa API LLM è disponibile per tutti, ma i tuoi template determinano la qualità.

Python 

# prompts.py - Sistema di template di prompt per ProseAI

class PromptTemplateEngine:
    """Gestisce i template di prompt per le diverse modalità di riscrittura."""

    TEMPLATES = {
        "summarize": {
            "name": "Summarize",
            "description": "Condensa il testo nei punti chiave",
            "system": ("You are an expert summarizer. Extract the core meaning "
                       "and key points. Preserve factual accuracy."),
            "instruction": ("Summarize the following text in {length} sentences. "
                            "Keep the most important facts and conclusions."),
            "defaults": {"length": "2-3"},
        },
        "formal": {
            "name": "Formal Tone",
            "description": "Riscrive in uno stile professionale e formale",
            "system": ("You are a professional editor specializing in formal "
                       "business and academic writing."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text in a formal, professional tone. "
                            "Use precise vocabulary, avoid contractions. "
                            "Preserve all factual content."),
            "defaults": {},
        },
        "casual": {
            "name": "Casual Tone",
            "description": "Riscrive in uno stile amichevole e colloquiale",
            "system": ("You are a friendly writer who makes complex topics "
                       "accessible and conversational."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text in a casual, friendly tone. "
                            "Use everyday language. Do not lose any key information."),
            "defaults": {},
        },
        "expand": {
            "name": "Expand",
            "description": "Approfondisce con maggiori dettagli ed esempi",
            "system": ("You are a thorough writer who enriches content with "
                       "relevant details and examples."),
            "instruction": ("Expand the following text to approximately {target_length}. "
                            "Add relevant details and examples. "
                            "Do not add speculative information."),
            "defaults": {"target_length": "twice the original length"},
        },
        "simplify": {
            "name": "Simplify",
            "description": "Riscrive per una lettura facile (livello 6a elementare)",
            "system": ("You are a plain-language expert. Rewrite text so that "
                       "a 12-year-old can understand it."),
            "instruction": ("Rewrite the following text at a {grade} reading level. "
                            "Use short sentences (under 15 words). "
                            "Replace jargon with simple words."),
            "defaults": {"grade": "6th grade"},
        },
    }

    def build_prompt(self, mode, user_text, **kwargs):
        """Costruisce un prompt completo per la modalità di riscrittura indicata."""
        if mode not in self.TEMPLATES:
            return {"error": f"Unknown mode: {mode}"}
        t = self.TEMPLATES[mode]
        params = dict(t["defaults"])
        params.update(kwargs)
        instruction = t["instruction"].format(**params)
        return {
            "mode": mode, "mode_name": t["name"],
            "messages": [
                {"role": "system", "content": t["system"]},
                {"role": "user", "content": f"{instruction}\
\
---\
\
{user_text}"},
            ],
        }

    def list_modes(self):
        return {k: {"name": t["name"], "description": t["description"],
                     "params": list(t["defaults"].keys())}
                for k, t in self.TEMPLATES.items()}

Parte 4: Risposte in Streaming

Gli utenti si aspettano di vedere il testo apparire parola per parola, come ChatGPT. Lo streaming migliora drasticamente la latenza percepita — invece di aspettare 5 secondi per una risposta completa, gli utenti vedono la prima parola in meno di 200ms. ProseAI usa i generatori Python e i Server-Sent Events (SSE) per trasmettere il testo riscritto al frontend in tempo reale.

Python 

# streaming.py - Generatore di risposte in streaming per ProseAI

import json
import re

class StreamingRewriter:
    """Generazione di testo in streaming usando il pattern generatore.
    In produzione, incapsula la risposta in streaming dell'API LLM."""

    def sse_format(self, data):
        """Formatta i dati come stringa Server-Sent Event."""
        return f"data: {json.dumps(data)}\
\
"

    def stream_rewrite(self, original, rewritten, mode):
        """Pipeline di streaming completa: start, tokens, done."""
        # 1. Evento di avvio
        yield self.sse_format({
            "type": "start", "mode": mode,
            "original_length": len(original.split()),
        })
        # 2. Streaming parola per parola
        words = rewritten.split()
        for i, word in enumerate(words):
            yield self.sse_format({
                "type": "token", "content": word + " ", "index": i,
            })
        # 3. Evento di fine con statistiche
        yield self.sse_format({
            "type": "done",
            "original_words": len(original.split()),
            "rewritten_words": len(words),
            "compression": round(len(words) / max(len(original.split()), 1), 2),
        })


# --- Demo ---
streamer = StreamingRewriter()

original = (
    "The implementation of machine learning algorithms in production "
    "environments necessitates careful consideration of computational "
    "resources, data pipeline architecture, and model versioning."
)
rewritten = (
    "Putting ML models into production means thinking about three things. "
    "First, you need enough computing power. Second, your data pipelines "
    "must be solid. Third, keep track of your model versions."
)

events = list(streamer.stream_rewrite(original, rewritten, "simplify"))
print(f"Total SSE events: {len(events)}")

# Analizza e visualizza

for event_str in events:
    data = json.loads(event_str.replace("data: ", "").strip())
    if data["type"] == "start":
        print(f"[START] Mode: {data['mode']}, Input: {data['original_length']} words")
    elif data["type"] == "token":
        output += data["content"]
    elif data["type"] == "done":
        print(f"[OUTPUT] {output.strip()}")
        print(f"[DONE] {data['original_words']} -> {data['rewritten_words']} words "
              f"({data['compression']}x)")

print(f"\
Sample SSE event:\

Parte 5: Il Server FastAPI

Questo è il cuore di ProseAI — il server API che unisce analisi, trasformazione, template di prompt e streaming. L'endpoint /api/rewrite supporta sia le normali risposte JSON sia lo streaming SSE tramite StreamingResponse.

app/main.py
"""ProseAI API Server - Text Composition and Rewriting SaaS."""
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Depends, Header
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
import uuid, time, asyncio

from .config import settings
from .analyzer import TextAnalyzer
from .transformer import TextTransformer
from .prompts import PromptTemplateEngine
from .streaming import StreamingRewriter

app = FastAPI(title="ProseAI API", version="1.0.0")
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory="static"), name="static")

analyzer = TextAnalyzer()
transformer = TextTransformer()
prompt_engine = PromptTemplateEngine()
streamer = StreamingRewriter()

class RewriteRequest(BaseModel):
    text: str = Field(..., min_length=10, max_length=10000)
    mode: str = Field(default="simplify")
    stream: bool = Field(default=False)
    params: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)

class AnalyzeRequest(BaseModel):
    text: str = Field(..., min_length=10, max_length=10000)

async def get_user(x_api_key: str = Header(...)):
    if not x_api_key:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="API key required")
    return {"id": "user_1", "tier": "pro"}

@app.get("/api/modes")
async def list_modes():
    return {"modes": prompt_engine.list_modes()}

@app.post("/api/analyze")
async def analyze_text(req: AnalyzeRequest):
    result = analyzer.analyze(req.text)
    result["reading_level"] = analyzer.reading_level_label(
        result["flesch_reading_ease"])
    return result

@app.post("/api/rewrite")
async def rewrite_text(req: RewriteRequest, user=Depends(get_user)):
    """Riscrive il testo nella modalità specificata. Supporta lo streaming via SSE."""
    prompt_data = prompt_engine.build_prompt(req.mode, req.text, **req.params)
    if "error" in prompt_data:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=prompt_data["error"])

    if req.stream:
        async def event_generator():
            # In produzione: streaming dall'API LLM usando prompt_data
            result = transformer.make_concise(req.text)
            for event in streamer.stream_rewrite(
                    req.text, result["text"], req.mode):
                yield event
                await asyncio.sleep(0.02)
        return StreamingResponse(event_generator(),
            media_type="text/event-stream",
            headers={"Cache-Control": "no-cache", "X-Accel-Buffering": "no"})

    # Senza streaming: restituisce la risposta JSON completa
    start = time.time()
    result = transformer.make_concise(req.text)
    return {
        "id": str(uuid.uuid4()), "mode": req.mode,
        "rewritten_text": result["text"],
        "analysis_before": analyzer.analyze(req.text),
        "analysis_after": analyzer.analyze(result["text"]),
        "processing_time": round(time.time() - start, 3),
    }

@app.get("/api/health")
async def health():
    return {"status": "ok", "service": "proseai"}

Parte 11: Collegati al Tuo Proprio LLM

Finora abbiamo usato API di terze parti. Ma il vero potenziale — e i veri margini — arrivano quando esegui i tuoi stessi modelli. Questo elimina i costi API per richiesta, ti dà pieno controllo su latenza e privacy, e ti permette di fare fine-tuning dei modelli per il tuo caso d'uso specifico.

Tre approcci principali per il self-hosting:

  • vLLM — massimo throughput, API compatibile con OpenAI, ideale per la produzione
  • Ollama — configurazione più semplice, ottimo per lo sviluppo e deployment su piccola scala
  • llama.cpp — il più leggero, funziona su CPU, ideale per il deployment su edge

Per la generazione di testo, fai self-hosting con vLLM, llama.cpp o Ollama:

Parte 13: Rate Limiting & Protezione API

Ogni SaaS in produzione ha bisogno di rate limiting per prevenire abusi, controllare i costi e garantire un uso equo. Ecco un'implementazione di livello produzione:

rate_limiter.py — Rate Limiting di Produzione per ProseAI
"""
Rate limiting di produzione per ProseAI.
Tre livelli: in-memory (sviluppo), Redis (produzione), token bucket (avanzato).
"""
import time
from collections import defaultdict

# === LIVELLO 1: Rate Limiter in Memoria (Sviluppo) ===
class InMemoryRateLimiter:
    """Semplice rate limiter a finestra scorrevole. Funziona per setup single-server."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.requests = defaultdict(list)

    def is_allowed(self, key, max_requests, window_seconds):
        """Controlla se la richiesta è consentita entro il rate limit."""
        now = time.time()
        window_start = now - window_seconds

        # Pulisce le voci vecchie
        self.requests[key] = [t for t in self.requests[key] if t > window_start]

        if len(self.requests[key]) >= max_requests:
            retry_after = self.requests[key][0] - window_start
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "limit": max_requests,
                "window": window_seconds,
                "retry_after": round(retry_after, 1),
                "current": len(self.requests[key])
            }}

        self.requests[key].append(now)
        return True, {{
            "remaining": max_requests - len(self.requests[key]),
            "limit": max_requests,
            "reset": round(window_start + window_seconds - now, 1)
        }}

# === LIVELLO 2: Rate Limiter Redis (Produzione) ===
class RedisRateLimiter:
    """Rate limiter basato su Redis per deployment distribuiti.

    In produzione, installa: pip install redis
    E usa una connessione Redis reale.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        # In produzione: self.redis = redis.Redis(host='redis', port=6379, db=0)
        self.memory = defaultdict(list)  # Simula Redis

    def check_rate_limit(self, user_id, tier="free"):
        """Controlla il rate limit in base al livello dell'utente."""
        limits = {{
            "free":       {{"requests_per_minute": 5,  "requests_per_day": 50}},
            "starter":    {{"requests_per_minute": 20, "requests_per_day": 500}},
            "pro":        {{"requests_per_minute": 60, "requests_per_day": 5000}},
            "enterprise": {{"requests_per_minute": 200, "requests_per_day": 50000}},
        }}

        tier_limits = limits.get(tier, limits["free"])
        now = time.time()

        # Controlla il limite per minuto
        minute_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:minute"
        self.memory[minute_key] = [t for t in self.memory[minute_key] if t > now - 60]

        if len(self.memory[minute_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_minute"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_minute",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"],
                "retry_after_seconds": 60 - (now - self.memory[minute_key][0])
            }}

        # Controlla il limite giornaliero
        day_key = f"rate:{{user_id}}:day"
        self.memory[day_key] = [t for t in self.memory[day_key] if t > now - 86400]

        if len(self.memory[day_key]) >= tier_limits["requests_per_day"]:
            return False, {{
                "error": "daily_limit_exceeded",
                "type": "per_day",
                "limit": tier_limits["requests_per_day"],
            }}

        # Consente la richiesta
        self.memory[minute_key].append(now)
        self.memory[day_key].append(now)

        return True, {{
            "remaining_minute": tier_limits["requests_per_minute"] - len(self.memory[minute_key]),
            "remaining_day": tier_limits["requests_per_day"] - len(self.memory[day_key]),
        }}

# === Middleware FastAPI ===
class RateLimitMiddleware:
    """
    Middleware FastAPI per il rate limiting.

    Utilizzo nella tua app:
        from rate_limiter import RateLimitMiddleware
        app.add_middleware(RateLimitMiddleware)

    Oppure come dipendenza:
        @app.get("/generate")
        async def generate(rate_limit: dict = Depends(check_rate_limit)):
            ...
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.limiter = RedisRateLimiter()

    def get_middleware_code(self):
        """Stampa il codice reale del middleware FastAPI."""
        code = "# Add to your FastAPI app:\
\
"
        code += "from fastapi import Request, Response\
"
        code += "from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware\
\
"
        code += "class RateLimitMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):\
"
        code += "    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):\
"
        code += "        api_key = request.headers.get('X-API-Key', 'anonymous')\
"
        code += "        user_id = self.get_user_from_key(api_key)\
"
        code += "        tier = self.get_user_tier(user_id)\
"
        code += "        allowed, info = self.limiter.check_rate_limit(user_id, tier)\
"
        code += "        if not allowed:\
"
        code += "            return JSONResponse(status_code=429, content=info)\
"
        code += "        response = await call_next(request)\
"
        code += "        response.headers['X-RateLimit-Remaining'] = str(info.get('remaining_minute', 0))\
"
        code += "        return response\
"
        print(code)

Punti Chiave

  • Analizza prima di trasformare: Misurare leggibilità, complessità delle frasi e frequenza delle parole ti dà metriche oggettive. Ti permette di mostrare agli utenti un confronto “prima vs. dopo” che dimostra il valore aggiunto dal tuo servizio.
  • Le trasformazioni basate su regole sono la tua rete di sicurezza: Semplificazione del vocabolario, rimozione di parole di riempimento e suddivisione delle frasi funzionano offline e non costano nulla. Usale come fallback quando le API LLM non sono disponibili.
  • I template di prompt sono il tuo fossato competitivo: La stessa API LLM è disponibile per tutti. I tuoi template di prompt costruiti con cura — con messaggi di sistema, istruzioni e vincoli — determinano qualità e coerenza.
  • Lo streaming è obbligatorio per i prodotti testuali: Gli utenti non aspetteranno 5–10 secondi fissando uno spinner. Lo streaming parola per parola via SSE fa sembrare il prodotto istantaneo e coinvolgente.
  • Separa nettamente le responsabilità: Analyzer, Transformer, PromptEngine e Streamer sono moduli indipendenti. Ognuno può essere testato, sostituito o aggiornato senza toccare gli altri.

Prossima lezione: In GenAI-4, costruisci un SaaS di Generazione di Codice — gestendo trasformazioni sensibili alla sintassi, supporto multi-linguaggio e sandbox sicure per l'esecuzione di codice.

GenAI-3 بناء: منتج AI SaaS

بناء منتج SaaS لتأليف النصوص وإعادة صياغتها

ابنِ ProseAI — خدمة جاهزة للإنتاج لإعادة صياغة النصوص وتأليفها بعدة أنماط: التلخيص والتوسيع والتبسيط وتغيير النبرة وترجمة الأسلوب. خلفية Python + FastAPI مع استجابات بثّية (streaming).
60 دقيقة متقدم / تطبيقي ستبني وتنشر منتجًا حقيقيًا

ما الذي ستبنيه

في هذا الدرس ستبني ProseAI — منتج SaaS لإعادة صياغة النصوص وتأليفها. يُرسل المستخدمون نصًا ويختارون نمط إعادة صياغة (تلخيص، توسيع، تبسيط، رسمي، عفوي)، وتقوم خدمتك بتحويل النص باستخدام قوالب موجّهات (prompt) مدعومة بنماذج اللغة الكبيرة (LLM) وخط أنابيب استجابة بثّية (streaming). ستنفّذ المكدّس الكامل: محرك تحليل النصوص، خط أنابيب التحويل، نظام قوالب الموجّهات، واجهة برمجة تطبيقات بثّية (API)، وواجهة أمامية مع معاينة حيّة.

ProseAI — نظرة شاملة على المشروع

المكوّن التقنية
خادم APIPython + FastAPI
تحليل النصوصتسجيل سهولة القراءة المخصّص، تحليل الجمل
تكامل LLMOpenAI API / Anthropic API (عبر قوالب الموجّهات)
البث (Streaming)Server-Sent Events (SSE) عبر FastAPI StreamingResponse
الواجهة الأماميةHTML + جافاسكربت خام مع معاينة بثّية حيّة
النشر (Deployment)Docker + أي مزوّد سحابي

هيكل المشروع

أنشئ هيكل المجلدات هذا على جهازك. سيُشرح كل ملف في هذا الدرس.

تخطيط المشروع
proseai/
├── app/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── main.py            # تطبيق FastAPI مع البث
│   ├── config.py          # الإعدادات ومفاتيح API
│   ├── models.py          # نماذج الطلب/الاستجابة من Pydantic
│   ├── analyzer.py        # محرك تحليل النصوص
│   ├── transformer.py     # خط أنابيب تحويل النصوص
│   ├── prompts.py         # قوالب الموجّهات لأنماط LLM
│   └── streaming.py       # مولّد الاستجابة البثّية
├── static/

├── requirements.txt
